experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs. Exps 0-4): a CARDINAL WEIGHT-MATCHING RIDGE built from duplicate moderate validities, with no zero-validity experts and no dominant top cue. Exp 4 dissociated VWEI from SDI structurally (50% experts are invisible to VWEI, penalized by SDI) and via 95%-anchored ceiling conflicts. This design instead engineers trials where VWEI's evidence sum is arithmetically pinned to ~0 by matching coalitions of moderate experts against single stronger experts, and dual trials where SDI's penalty difference is pinned to ~0 by matching endorsement counts. The validities [0.90, 0.85, 0.80, 0.80, 0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.65, 0.60] are chosen so that VWEI's amplified log-odds weights satisfy 2*w(0.75) = w(0.80) exactly at gamma = ln2/ln(1.2616) = 2.98 and 4*w(0.75) = w(0.85) exactly at gamma = ln4/ln(1.579) = 3.03 -- both crossing points sit at the CENTER of VWEI's own gamma box [2.8, 3.2], so the weight-matching holds (|E| <= 0.53, hence P within +/-2.5 points of 0.50) across the ENTIRE parameter box, verified at gamma in {2.8, 3.0, 3.2} x beta in {0.18, 0.23}. 12 base pairs, each exactly A/B-mirrored (24 unique pairs, K = 96//24 = 4, 96 trials, 8 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. FAMILY 1 -- EVIDENCE-MATCHED COUNT GRADIENT (pairs 1-5): one option carries 1 (or 2) endorsements, the other carries a weight-matched coalition of 2-4 moderate experts (e.g., A = {85%} vs B = {80%, 75%, 75%}: E = 5.22 - 5.32 = -0.10). VWEI is pinned at chance: P(fewer-endorsement option) = 0.49-0.50 on all five pairs (box range 0.48-0.52) -- it has no mechanism, at any gamma/beta/epsilon in its box, for these stimuli to move it off a guess, because its cardinal weights cancel by construction. SDI climbs monotonically with endorsement-count difference: 0.69 (1v2), 0.70 (1v2, second realization), 0.83 (1v3), 0.83 (2v4), 0.89 (1v4) (box ranges 0.65-0.73 up to 0.86-0.92), since every net endorsement adds ~0.96 penalty units and its D strictly increases with count difference -- the slope sign is parameter-independent. Any systematic departure from 50% toward the fewer-endorsement option on pairs 1-5 falsifies VWEI; flatness at 50% falsifies SDI. FAMILY 2 -- COUNT-MATCHED VALIDITY-GAP GRADIENT (pairs 6-9): exactly one endorsement per side, with the endorser validity gap shrinking (.90 vs .60; .85 vs .65; .85 vs .80; .80 vs .75). SDI is pinned at 0.50-0.52 on all four (its penalty weights (1-v)^delta span <5% across the whole validity range at delta <= 0.05, and the alpha tie-break adds at most 3 points) -- structurally near-blind to WHO endorses at matched counts. VWEI sweeps 0.89 -> 0.73 -> 0.62 -> 0.56 (box ranges 0.84-0.95 down to 0.55-0.59), a 33-point monotone gradient in endorser validity that no SDI parameterization can produce. FAMILY 3 -- SIGN CONFLICT AT THE RIDGE CREST (pair 10): four 75% experts (total weight 5.30) vs one 80% expert (weight 2.66). VWEI: majority for the 4-endorsement coalition, P(A) = 0.63 (box 0.61-0.65). SDI: majority for the single endorsement, P(A) = 0.10 (box 0.08-0.12) -- opposite majorities, both far from chance, sign-robust across both boxes. BASELINE/SUB-RIDGE (pairs 11-12): pair 11 ({90%} vs {65%, 60%}) is the one agreement cell (VWEI 0.89, SDI 0.71 -- both prefer A, calibrating each theory's scale where they concur); pair 12 ({80%, 75%} vs {85%}) sits just BELOW the matching ridge (VWEI 0.43, SDI 0.30 -- both prefer B but at parametrically distinct depths, gap >= 9 points across boxes). THE DOUBLE DISSOCIATION IS UN-FAKEABLE: the two theories are placed in orthogonal indifference regimes -- VWEI is indifferent exactly when endorsement counts differ at matched evidence (Family 1), SDI is indifferent exactly when counts match but validity composition differs (Family 2) -- and no reparameterization of either theory can escape its own indifference condition (VWEI's weights cancel by arithmetic fixed at gamma ~ 3; SDI's penalty weights are count-driven and validity-flat by delta <= 0.05). A VWEI subject is a flat 50% line across the entire count gradient and a steep monotone curve across the gap gradient; an SDI subject is a steep monotone climb across the count gradient and a flat ~51% line across the gap gradient, plus a strong majority for the single endorser on pair 10 where VWEI favors the coalition. All pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating cues; no all-tie pairs; no pair leaves both theories guessing), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Double-dissociation composite built on the two strongest contrasts
    # engineered into this design:
    #
    # COMPONENT 1 ("big-gap single endorsers", pairs 6/18, 8 trials/subject):
    #   both options carry exactly ONE endorsement; the endorsers' validities
    #   differ by >= 0.25 (0.90 vs 0.60).  VWEI overwhelmingly follows the
    #   higher-validity endorser (P ~ 0.89 across its whole parameter box);
    #   SDI is structurally near-blind at matched endorsement counts
    #   (P ~ 0.50-0.55 across its whole box).
    #
    # COMPONENT 2 ("ridge-crest coalition", pairs 10/22, 8 trials/subject):
    #   one option carries a single 0.80-validity endorsement, the other a
    #   coalition of four 0.75-validity endorsements.  Score +1 for choosing
    #   the COALITION.  VWEI favors the coalition (P ~ 0.62); SDI strongly
    #   favors the single endorser (coalition P ~ 0.10).
    #
    # Metric = mean of the two rates.  Expected: VWEI ~ 0.75, SDI ~ 0.31.
    # Both components use only 8 trials each but their gaps point the SAME
    # way after sign alignment, so the composite has a large mean gap and
    # modest binomial-only between-subject variance.

    V = np.array([0.90, 0.85, 0.80, 0.80, 0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.65, 0.60])

    a_cells = data['option_a_ratings'].tolist()
    b_cells = data['option_b_ratings'].tolist()
    resp = data['response'].to_numpy()

    scores_gap = []    # 1 = chose the higher-validity single endorser
    scores_coal = []    # 1 = chose the 4x0.75 coalition over the single 0.80 endorser

    for a_raw, b_raw, r in zip(a_cells, b_cells, resp):
        a = np.asarray(a_raw, dtype=float).ravel()
        b = np.asarray(b_raw, dtype=float).ravel()
        if a.shape != V.shape or b.shape != V.shape:
            continue
        ca = int(round(a.sum()))
        cb = int(round(b.sum()))
        chose_a = (int(r) == 0)

        if ca == 1 and cb == 1:
            # Single endorsement on each side: who endorsed, and how good
            # is that expert?
            ia = int(np.argmax(a))
            ib = int(np.argmax(b))
            va = V[ia]
            vb = V[ib]
            if abs(va - vb) >= 0.25:
                hi_is_a = (va > vb)
                scores_gap.append(1.0 if (chose_a == hi_is_a) else 0.0)

        elif (ca == 1 and cb == 4) or (ca == 4 and cb == 1):
            # Ridge-crest conflict: verify it is exactly the designed cell
            # (single 0.80 expert vs four 0.75 experts) and score the
            # coalition choice.
            if ca == 1:
                single_vec, coal_vec = a, b
                single_is_a = True
            else:
                single_vec, coal_vec = b, a
                single_is_a = False
            i_single = int(np.argmax(single_vec))
            coal_idx = np.where(coal_vec > 0.5)[0]
            if (
                abs(V[i_single] - 0.80) < 1e-9
                and len(coal_idx) == 4
                and bool(np.all(np.abs(V[coal_idx] - 0.75) < 1e-9))
            ):
                # +1 when the subject chose the coalition side
                scores_coal.append(1.0 if (chose_a != single_is_a) else 0.0)

    r_gap = float(np.mean(scores_gap)) if len(scores_gap) > 0 else 0.5
    r_coal = float(np.mean(scores_coal)) if len(scores_coal) > 0 else 0.5
    return 0.5 * (r_gap + r_coal)
metric.rationale: The design's double dissociation is exploited at its two strongest, sign-aligned points. COMPONENT 1 uses the count-matched big-validity-gap trials (pairs 6/18: a single 0.90 endorsement vs a single 0.60 endorsement, 8 trials per subject). Here VWEI's amplified log-odds weights produce P(follow the 0.90 expert) ≈ 0.84-0.94 across its entire (gamma, beta, epsilon) box, while SDI is pinned near chance (0.50-0.55) because its penalty difference at equal endorsement counts is driven only by delta ≤ 0.05 and alpha ≤ 0.05 — it is structurally near-blind to WHO endorses when counts match. COMPONENT 2 uses the ridge-crest conflict (pairs 10/22: four 0.75 experts vs one 0.80 expert, 8 trials per subject), scored +1 for choosing the coalition. VWEI's evidence sum favors the coalition (P ≈ 0.61-0.65 box-wide, since 4*w(0.75) > w(0.80) at gamma ≈ 3), while SDI's penalty difference of ~3 units at beta ≈ 1 drives P(coalition) ≈ 0.08-0.12 box-wide. Averaging the two aligned rates yields an expected pooled value of ~0.75 under VWEI vs ~0.31 under SDI — a ~0.44 mean gap. Between-subject variance is essentially binomial (each component uses 8 trials; var of the average ≈ 0.01 for both theories), so at N = 25 the Welch t-statistic is expected around 15 (p << 0.001). The metric is a plain choice rate on structurally identified trial cells (no theory fitting, no likelihood evaluation), works identically on the pooled DataFrame and on single-subject slices, avoids hashing any sequence-valued column, and degrades gracefully to 0.5 if a cell is somehow absent. Note the sign alignment is essential: both components are scored in the direction VWEI predicts (follow the strong expert; follow the weight-matched coalition), so the two gaps add rather than cancel.

proposer_theory.description: Validity-Weighted Evidence Integration (VWEI) with subjective validity amplification. On each trial the decision maker computes, for every rating dimension j, the discriminant d_j = sign(a_j - b_j) in {-1, 0, +1}, weights it by a subjectively amplified validity w_j = [log(v_j/(1-v_j))]^gamma, and accumulates evidence E = sum_j w_j * d_j. Choice probability is a sigmoid of beta * E mixed with a small uniform lapse epsilon. gamma = 1 recovers Bayes-optimal log-odds integration; gamma -> infinity recovers Take-The-Best; the empirically human region sits at gamma near 3, where the top cue dominates coalitions of weaker cues on steep validity gradients (Exp 2) but lower cues still attenuate allegiance on shallow gradients (Exp 1). This round's refinement is purely parametric: the mechanism is unchanged, but the sampling region is re-centered on the hand-verified sweet spot (gamma = 3, beta = 0.2, epsilon = 0), the lapse range is restored to (a tightened version of) the arbiter's [0, 0.2], and the beta floor is raised so that generic flattening noise no longer competes with the gamma-structured weight profile for attenuation work.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Validity-Weighted Evidence Integration (VWEI) with subjective
    # validity amplification. Stimulus is the pair of option feature
    # vectors for the current trial: array-like of shape
    # (2, n_features), row 0 = option A, row 1 = option B.
    #
    # Evidence for A over B:  E = sum_j w_j * sign(a_j - b_j),
    # with w_j = [log(v_j / (1 - v_j))]^gamma.
    #   gamma = 1  -> Bayes-optimal log-odds weighting (full integration)
    #   gamma -> inf -> Take-The-Best (top cue dominates every coalition)
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * E), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are communicated in the
    # instructions, so weights are fixed for the whole block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"VWEI expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Guard the log-odds against v = 1 (infinite weight) and v < 0.5.
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5 + 1e-9, 1.0 - 1e-6)
    log_odds = np.log(v / (1.0 - v))

    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # Subjective cue weights: amplified log-odds validity.
    w = np.sign(log_odds) * np.abs(log_odds) ** gamma

    # Per-cue discriminant: +1 favors A, -1 favors B, 0 is uninformative.
    d = np.sign(a - b)

    # Accumulated evidence for A (positive) vs B (negative).
    E = float(np.dot(w, d))

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # When E == 0 this is exactly 0.5 (uniform guessing), for any beta.
    x = beta * E
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
proposer_theory.rationale: The critic confirmed the VWEI mechanism family is correct (accepted, loss 0.1040) and diagnosed the failure as parametric: the sampler was using generic flattening (wide epsilon up to 0.45, beta down to 0.1) to do attenuation work that the gamma-structured weight profile should do, which simultaneously dragged Exp 2 toward chance (-0.19 vs -0.256) and inflated between-subject variance there (0.0392 vs 0.0128). The fix is a pure parameter-range edit; predict/policy are unchanged. (1) I first carried out the verification the critic requested: enumerating every conflict trial in both experiments and computing E and P(choice) by hand at gamma=3, beta=0.2, epsilon=0. Exp 1 (log-odds weights 2.20/1.39/0.85/0.41/0, cubed to 10.60/2.66/0.61/0.07/0) gives per-trial allegiances of ~0.81 (8 trials), ~0.60 (4 trials), ~0.53 (2 trials), averaging to 0.710 vs the real 0.7117. Exp 2 (log-odds 2.94/2.20/1.74/0.62/0.41/0, cubed to 25.5/10.6/5.22/0.24/0.07/0) gives mean P(tally winner) = 0.244, i.e. metric -0.256 vs the real -0.2562. The sweet spot is verified and essentially exact. (2) I therefore re-centered every range on that point: gamma in [2.8, 3.2] (steepened well above the old floor of 1.0, per the critic's 2.5-3.5 guidance, but tightened around 3 so no sampled subject lands in the flat-Bayes region that produces the wrong sign on Exp 2), beta in [0.18, 0.23] (floor raised from 0.1 toward the critic's 0.2-0.3, ceiling kept low because beta=0.6 with gamma=2.5 provably overshoots Exp 1 to ~0.82), and epsilon narrowed to [0, 0.03] — within the arbiter's [0, 0.2] and far below my previous [0, 0.45], since the data show almost no lapse-type noise beyond what beta already provides. (3) Averaging the closed-form per-trial allegiances uniformly over these boxes yields expected metrics of approximately (0.706, -0.250) vs real (0.7117, -0.2562) — an L2 error of roughly 0.01, an order of magnitude below the current floor of 0.1040. The tightened ranges also shrink the between-subject spread of the Exp 2 metric from the too-heterogeneous 0.039 toward the real 0.0128. The mechanism itself remains fully experiment-invariant: it consumes only the experiment-provided validities, guesses exactly when E = 0, and retains graded sensitivity to coalition size and cue validity wherever TTB is flat.

next_theory.description: Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS), a.k.a. Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration. Subjects treat every expert endorsement not as an asset but as a liability whose magnitude scales with the endorser's claimed validity: a highly valid expert's praise is a strong claim, and strong claims attract the most suspicion. On each trial the decision maker computes a penalty for each option, P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), where c0 is a flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure unweighted defect counting) and c1 * v_j^kappa is the confidence-distrust term, with penalty INCREASING in the endorser's validity and kappa controlling how steeply. The subject chooses the lower-penalty option via P(A) = sigmoid(beta * (P(B) - P(A))) mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon. History is ignored because validities are communicated in the instructions, so skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block. VPS reproduces the sign of every observed metric while fixing the one structural blind spot of pure defect counting (SDI): on matched-count trials with a large validity gap (e.g., a single 0.90 endorser vs a single 0.60 endorser), SDI is pinned at 0.5 while VPS predicts a clear majority for the LOWER-validity endorser — exactly what the Experiment 6 composite (observed 0.193) requires.
next_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS) /
    # Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration.
    #
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Each endorsement is a LIABILITY whose magnitude scales with the
    # endorser's claimed validity (a strong claim attracts suspicion):
    #   penalty for option X:  P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa)
    #     c0        -> flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure
    #                  unweighted endorsement counting)
    #     c1*v^kappa -> confidence-distrust term, INCREASING in validity
    # Decision variable:  D = P(B) - P(A)   (positive favors A)
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * D), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so the
    # skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"VPS expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Validities live in [0.5, 1.0]; clip defensively (no logarithms
    # are taken, so v = 1 is harmless here).
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0)

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])

    # Per-endorser liability: flat suspicion plus a
    # validity-proportional confidence-distrust charge.
    d = c0 + c1 * (v ** kappa)

    # Total accumulated suspicion for each option.
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # D > 0 favors A (B carries more accumulated suspicion than A).
    D = pen_b - pen_a

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # D == 0 (exact tie in penalties) -> exactly 0.5.
    x = beta * D
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
next_theory.rationale: The arbiter diagnosed VWEI's failures (endorsements treated as assets, insensitivity to 50%-expert endorsements, positive evidence slopes) and prescribed a brand-new competitor to SDI: Validity-Proportional Skepticism. I implement that mechanism faithfully. (1) Core mechanism: penalty P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), choice = lower penalty via sigmoid(beta*(P(B)-P(A))) with lapse epsilon. The c1*v^kappa term is the key innovation over SDI's (1-v)^delta: because the penalty INCREASES with validity, a highly valid expert's endorsement is the most suspicious claim of all. (2) Hand-verified behavior at the range center (kappa=2, beta=2, epsilon=0.1, c0=0.1, c1=1): Exp 1 — the TTB winner carries fewer endorsements, so its penalty is lower; typical penalty gaps of ~0.3-0.9 give P(TTB winner) ~0.65-0.70 against the observed 0.7117, slightly better than SDI's overshoot (0.7792). Exp 2 — the tally winner's larger endorsing coalition drowns in accumulated penalty, so P(choose tally winner | conflict) sits well below 0.5, matching the observed -0.2562. Exp 3 — on HIGH trials the 0.90-expert endorsement carries the single largest penalty, so the TTB winner is AVOIDED; on LOW trials the opposing multi-endorsement coalition accumulates more penalty, so the TTB winner is FOLLOWED; the contrast is strongly negative (~-0.5), matching the observed -0.5467 where SDI undershot (-0.415). Exp 4 — more validity-weighted evidence behind the TTB winner means higher-validity endorsements means higher penalty, producing the negative signed-evidence slope (observed -0.1938). Exp 5 — the top-cue option is always the endorsement-majority option and its 0.95 endorsement carries the largest single penalty, so it is strongly avoided (~0.11-0.15), matching the observed 0.1143. Exp 6 — the crucial improvement over SDI: on matched-count single-endorser trials the 0.90 endorser is penalized more than the 0.60 endorser (c0 + c1*0.81 vs c0 + c1*0.36 at kappa=2), pulling the gap component below 0.5 (~0.35-0.40) where SDI is structurally pinned at ~0.5; the coalition component stays low (~0.05-0.10), so the composite lands near ~0.20-0.23 versus the observed 0.1925 (SDI: 0.304). (3) Parameter ranges are centered on the arbiter's hand-verified sweet spot but kept wide enough to express genuine between-subject heterogeneity; every parameter appears in predict and every declared parameter is used. (4) Falsifiability: VPS separates from SDI on a sharp axis — matched endorsement counts with graded validity gaps (VPS: monotone preference for weaker endorsers; SDI: flat ~0.5) — and from VWEI everywhere VWEI failed, since endorsements are liabilities, 50%-expert endorsements still carry penalty c0 + c1*0.5^kappa > 0, and validity-weighted evidence behind an option REDUCES the probability it is chosen.

experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs. Exps 0-5): the first head-to-head between the two DEFECT-INTEGRATION theories. SDI and VPS agree that every endorsement is a liability, but they disagree about the WEIGHT PROFILE attached to the endorser's validity: SDI's skepticism weight (1-v)^delta is nearly FLAT across the whole validity range (0.86-0.98 at delta <= 0.05, a <14% spread; at delta=0 exactly flat), so SDI is essentially a validity-blind endorsement COUNTER; VPS's weight c0 + c1*v^kappa INCREASES steeply in validity (a 0.95 expert's endorsement costs ~2.9x a 0.50 expert's at mid parameters), so VPS actively prefers options endorsed by WEAKER experts. The design places the two theories in orthogonal indifference regimes: SDI is pinned at chance exactly when endorsement counts match but validity composition differs; VPS is pinned at (near) chance exactly when counts differ but its validity-scaled penalties cancel. Validities (15 experts): [0.95, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90, 0.85, 0.80, 0.65, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.55, 0.50, 0.50, 0.50, 0.50] -- duplicates are required to build coalitions; the spread 0.50-0.95 spans the full range. 12 base pairs, each exactly A/B-mirrored (24 unique pairs, K = 96//24 = 4, 96 trials, 8 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. All predictions below are given as P(A) at SDI mid-params (delta=.025, beta=1, eps=.115, alpha=.025) and VPS mid-params (kappa=2, beta=2, eps=.10, c0=.1, c1=1), with full-box ranges verified sign-robust. FAMILY 1 -- VALIDITY-GAP LADDER AT MATCHED COUNTS (pairs 1-5): 1v1 pairs with shrinking endorser gaps (.95/.50, .90/.55, .85/.60, .80/.65) plus the doubled 2v2 max-gap pair (.95+.90 vs .55+.50). VPS predicts a monotone ladder BELOW 50%: 0.24, 0.29, 0.34, 0.40, 0.13 -- it always prefers the LOWER-validity endorser, structurally (its penalty is strictly increasing in v for any c1>0, so D<0 at matched counts for EVERY parameterization). SDI is pinned at 0.51 +/- 0.02 (box 0.50-0.56): its penalty weights vary <14% and its only tilt, the alpha<=0.05 tie-break, pushes TOWARD the high-validity endorser -- i.e., AWAY from VPS's prediction, so no SDI parameterization can mimic the ladder. A monotone descending P(A) in gap falsifies SDI; a flat ~0.51 line falsifies VPS. FAMILY 2 -- SIGN CONFLICTS, OPPOSITE MAJORITIES (pairs 6-8): (a) 3x0.50 vs 2x0.90: VPS 0.79 (box 0.60-0.90) vs SDI 0.26 (box 0.24-0.30); (b) 4x0.50 vs 3x0.90: VPS 0.89 (box 0.75-0.93) vs SDI 0.25 (box 0.26-0.31); (c) 2x0.90 vs 3x0.60: VPS 0.31 (box 0.17-0.45) vs SDI 0.72 (box 0.68-0.75). Every conflict is sign-robust across BOTH entire parameter boxes (e.g., pair 6: VPS D = -c0 + c1(2*0.9^kappa - 3*0.5^kappa) > 0 always since c0/c1 <= 0.214 < 0.700; pair 8: D < 0 always since c0/c1 <= 0.214 < 0.365). A single majority choice on any conflict cell adjudicates the theories with no free parameters able to reverse it. FAMILY 3 -- JUNK-COUNT GRADIENT VS FIXED 2x0.90 (pairs 9, 10, 6): k = 1, 2, 3 endorsements from 50% experts on A against the same two 90% endorsements on B. SDI declines 0.66 -> 0.45 -> 0.26, CROSSING 50% between k=1 and k=2 (each junk endorsement adds ~0.97 penalty units; crossing at count parity is structural). VPS declines only 0.91 -> 0.86 -> 0.79 and does NOT cross through k=3, because each 0.50 endorsement costs only ~0.35 penalty units vs ~0.91 for a 0.90 endorsement -- it takes ~2.5 junk endorsements to offset one 90% endorsement for VPS but only 1 for SDI. The LOCATION OF THE CROSSING POINT is the quantitative signature. FAMILY 4 -- INDIFFERENCE ASYMMETRY (pairs 11-12): pair 11 (one 0.90 vs two 0.60s) is engineered so 2*0.6^kappa ~= 0.9^kappa (within 0.04-0.19 across kappa in [1.6, 2.4]), with the c0 count term partially cancelling the residual: VPS's D ranges only [-0.20, +0.20] over its ENTIRE box, keeping P(A) in [0.40, 0.61] (mid 0.50) -- near chance -- while SDI delivers a clear majority, P(A) = 0.70 (box 0.65-0.71), because B carries one extra endorsement. Pair 12 (3x0.90 vs 2x0.50) is the floor test: both theories prefer B, but SDI only moderately (P(A) = 0.35, box 0.28-0.42) while VPS is pinned at the floor (P(A) = 0.07, box 0.04-0.10) -- a 25+-point magnitude gap where sign cannot adjudicate. THE DISSOCIATION IS UN-FAKEABLE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a VPS subject is a descending ladder in Family 1 (all rungs < 0.47), stays above 0.60 through k=3 in Family 3, and sits at chance on pair 11; an SDI subject is a flat ~0.51 line across the entire ladder (its alpha tie-break can only push it ABOVE 0.5, opposite to VPS), crosses 50% at k=2 in Family 3, and shows a 0.70 majority on pair 11. Because SDI's stimulus-driven variation at matched counts is bounded by alpha*delta-logit <= 0.25 penalty units while VPS's ladder spans D in [-1.6, -0.41], and because VPS's indifference on pair 11 is arithmetic (2*0.6^kappa ~= 0.9^kappa across its kappa box) while SDI's count signal there is a full penalty unit, neither theory's parameter box can approximate the other's profile. All pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating endorsements, no all-tie pairs, no pair where both theories guess -- the closest, pair 11, is precisely the cell where they maximally diverge), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # "Validity-following rate in theory-conflict cells"
    #
    # The 15 experts split into a HIGH-validity group (features 0-6:
    # validities 0.95, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90, 0.85, 0.80, 0.65) and a
    # LOW-validity group (features 7-14: validity 0.60). Every trial in
    # this design pits a "pure high" option against a "pure low"
    # option. Two families of cells separate SDI from VPS:
    #
    # Family 1 (matched endorsement counts, validity gap): SDI's
    #   penalty is a near-flat function of validity (delta ~ 0), so it
    #   is pinned at ~0.51 for the high-validity option (its weak
    #   alpha tie-break even pushes slightly ABOVE 0.5). VPS's
    #   penalty rises steeply in validity, so it systematically picks
    #   the LOW-validity option (~0.28).
    #
    # Family 2 (count conflict where the FEWER-endorsed option is the
    #   high-validity one): SDI follows the endorsement count and
    #   picks the high-validity option (~0.72). VPS's validity-scaled
    #   distrust makes the low-validity majority cheaper, so it picks
    #   the high-validity option only ~0.30 of the time.
    #
    # The metric is the average of P(choose the high-validity-group
    #   option) over these two families. SDI predicts ~0.62; VPS
    #   predicts ~0.29.

    V = np.array([0.95, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90, 0.85, 0.80, 0.65,
                  0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60])

    f1_hits = 0.0
    f1_n = 0
    f2_hits = 0.0
    f2_n = 0

    for a_raw, b_raw, r in zip(data['option_a_ratings'],
                               data['option_b_ratings'],
                               data['response']):
        a = np.asarray(a_raw, dtype=float).ravel()
        b = np.asarray(b_raw, dtype=float).ravel()
        m = int(min(a.size, b.size, V.size))
        if m == 0:
            continue
        a = a[:m]
        b = b[:m]

        top = V[:m] >= 0.65  # high-validity expert group
        a_top = float(np.sum(a[top]))
        a_bot = float(np.sum(a[~top]))
        b_top = float(np.sum(b[top]))
        b_bot = float(np.sum(b[~top]))

        # Require each option to be endorsed purely by one group
        # (all trials in this design satisfy this; guards oddities).
        if (a_top > 0 and a_bot > 0) or (b_top > 0 and b_bot > 0):
            continue
        ca = a_top + a_bot
        cb = b_top + b_bot
        if ca == 0 or cb == 0:
            continue

        a_is_top = a_top > 0
        b_is_top = b_top > 0
        if a_is_top == b_is_top:
            continue

        chose_a = (int(round(float(r))) == 0)
        chose_top = chose_a if a_is_top else (not chose_a)

        if ca == cb:
            # Family 1: matched counts, validity gap.
            f1_n += 1
            f2_unused = None
            f1_hits += 1.0 if chose_top else 0.0
        else:
            # Family 2: count conflict; keep only cells where the
            # FEWER-endorsed option is the high-validity one
            # (the cells where SDI and VPS point in opposite
            # directions). Cells where the fewer-endorsed option is
            # the low-validity one are agreed upon by both theories
            # and are excluded.
            fewer_is_top = (a_is_top and ca < cb) or (b_is_top and cb < ca)
            if fewer_is_top:
                f2_n += 1
                f2_hits += 1.0 if chose_top else 0.0

    p1 = f1_hits / f1_n if f1_n > 0 else np.nan
    p2 = f2_hits / f2_n if f2_n > 0 else np.nan
    vals = [p for p in (p1, p2) if not np.isnan(p)]
    if not vals:
        return 0.5
    return float(np.mean(vals))
metric.rationale: The design's experts split cleanly into a high-validity group (features 0-6, validities 0.65-0.95) and a low-validity group (features 7-14, validity 0.60), and every trial pits a pure-high option against a pure-low option. This yields two orthogonal conflict families. FAMILY 1 (matched endorsement counts, 12 unique pairs, 48 trials/subject: e.g. one 0.95 endorser vs one 0.60 endorser; 2x0.90 vs 2x0.60): SDI's skepticism weight (1-v)^delta is nearly flat over the validity range (delta in [0, 0.05]), so its penalty difference is ~0 and its weak alpha tie-break pushes it slightly TOWARD the high-validity option (P ~ 0.51-0.55). VPS's penalty c0 + c1*v^kappa rises steeply in validity, so it systematically prefers the LOW-validity option (P(high) ~ 0.28 at mid parameters, and < 0.47 across its entire parameter box since D = c1*(v_lo^kappa - v_hi^kappa) < 0 structurally). FAMILY 2 (count conflicts where the FEWER-endorsed option is the high-validity one, 8 unique pairs, 32 trials/subject: 3x0.60 vs 2x0.90; 4x0.60 vs 3x0.90; 2x0.90 vs 3x0.60; 1x0.90 vs 2x0.60): SDI follows the endorsement count and picks the high-validity option with P ~ 0.70-0.73; VPS finds the low-validity majority cheaper per endorsement and picks the high-validity option only ~0.14-0.50 of the time (mean ~0.30). Cells where the fewer-endorsed option is the LOW-validity one (trials 9, 12, 21, 24) are agreed upon by both theories and are deliberately excluded so they cannot dilute the contrast. The metric averages P(choose the high-validity-group option) over the two families: SDI predicts ~0.62, VPS predicts ~0.29 — a gap of ~0.33 with per-subject standard deviation of only ~0.05 (binomial noise over 48 + 32 trials), giving a Welch t-statistic around 20 at N=25 (p << 0.001). The contrast is sign-robust across both theories' full parameter boxes: even at VPS's most SDI-like corner (c0=0.15, c1=0.7, kappa=1.6, beta=1.6, eps=0.13) the composite only rises to ~0.40, while SDI's least favorable corner stays ~0.59. The metric uses only the high/low validity grouping (threshold 0.65), which is invariant to the exact validities assigned to features 7-14, and it is well-defined both on the pooled DataFrame and on any single subject's 96-trial slice.

proposer_theory.description: Skeptical Defect Integration (SDI). Subjects do not treat an expert's positive rating ('1') as an asset; they treat it as a liability — an endorsement from a fallible expert is noise-laden, adverse evidence. On each trial the decision maker computes a penalty for each option, P(X) = sum_j d_j * x_j, where d_j = (1 - v_j)^delta is the skepticism weight attached to expert j (delta = 0 recovers pure unweighted defect counting — every endorsement is one unit of suspicion; larger delta discounts endorsements from low-validity experts more steeply, since a bad expert's praise is especially untrustworthy). The subject chooses the option with the LOWER total penalty, i.e., the option that attracted less endorsement. Choice probability is P(A) = sigmoid(beta * (P(B) - P(A))) mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon. Exact penalty ties are broken by a weak validity-weighted endorsement term alpha * sum_j logit(v_j) * (a_j - b_j), which captures residual heterogeneity: as alpha grows, SDI smoothly recovers VWEI-like endorsement-following behavior. The empirically human region sits at delta near 0 (near-pure defect counting) with moderate noise. SDI is the only account in this domain that reproduces the SIGN of every observed metric: it follows the TTB winner whenever the tally winner carries a larger endorsing coalition (Exp 1 metric positive), follows the tally loser / top-cue favorite when the tally winner has more endorsements (Exp 2 metric negative), prefers the option with fewer endorsements even when a dominant high-validity cue endorses the rival (Exp 3 metric strongly negative, HIGH minus LOW), and produces a negative signed-evidence slope because P(choose TTB winner) DECREASES as validity-weighted evidence accumulates behind the more-endorsed option (Exp 4). It makes a novel falsifiable prediction: on designs where the high-validity option carries MORE positive ratings than the low-validity option, SDI predicts majority choices OPPOSITE to both TTB and VWEI.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Skeptical Defect Integration (SDI).
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Penalty for option X:  P(X) = sum_j d_j * x_j,
    #   d_j = (1 - v_j)^delta  (skepticism weight; delta = 0 -> pure
    #   unweighted defect counting).
    # Decision variable:      D = (P(B) - P(A)) + alpha * E,
    #   E = sum_j logit(v_j) * (a_j - b_j)  (weak validity-weighted
    #   endorsement tie-break).
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * D), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are communicated in the
    # instructions, so skepticism weights are fixed for the block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SDI expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Guard against v = 1 (infinite logit) and v < 0.5.
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5 + 1e-9, 1.0 - 1e-6)

    delta = float(parameters["delta"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    alpha = float(parameters["alpha"])

    # Skepticism weights: an endorsement from expert j is a liability,
    # scaled by how fallible the expert is.
    d = (1.0 - v) ** delta

    # Total penalty (accumulated suspicion) for each option.
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # Weak validity-weighted endorsement term (tie-break only).
    w = np.log(v / (1.0 - v))
    endorse = float(np.dot(w, a - b))

    # D > 0 favors A (A carries fewer / more-heavily-discounted
    # liabilities than B, plus a small endorsement edge).
    D = (pen_b - pen_a) + alpha * endorse

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # D == 0 (exact tie in penalties and endorsement) -> exactly 0.5.
    x = beta * D
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
proposer_theory.rationale: The arbiter diagnosed that both TTB (pi_1) and VWEI (pi_3) fail on the dissociation designs: TTB is structurally flat on the Exp-3 validity-sensitivity contrast (real -0.5467 vs 0.01) and on the Exp-4 signed-evidence slope (real -0.1938 vs 0.0002), while VWEI gets the wrong sign on both. SDI fixes this mechanistically: because the tally winner ALWAYS carries strictly more positive ratings than the tally loser (wins differ by exactly the difference in endorsement counts), a subject who minimizes endorsements is anti-tallying on every conflict trial, which (i) tracks the TTB winner in Exp 1 (predicted ~0.72-0.78 vs real 0.7117; pi_1 erred +0.13), (ii) produces a strongly negative allegiance metric in Exp 2 (~-0.28 vs real -0.2562, near-exact), (iii) produces a strongly negative HIGH-minus-LOW contrast in Exp 3 (~-0.42 vs real -0.5467 — the HIGH pairs are exactly those where a lone dominant cue endorses one option against a smaller or zero opposing coalition, so SDI picks the UNendorsed rival; pi_1 was off by 0.56, pi_3 by 0.99), and (iv) produces a negative signed-evidence slope in Exp 4 (~-0.21 vs real -0.1938, near-exact), because P(choose TTB winner) falls as validity-weighted evidence piles up behind the more-endorsed option. Hand simulation of the full parameter box confirms the SIGN of every metric is invariant across the declared ranges, so the fit is robust to per-subject parameter heterogeneity (unlike pi_3, whose sign flips with gamma). I tightened the arbiter's suggested box (delta [0,2]->[0,0.05], beta [0.3,1.5]->[0.9,1.1], epsilon [0,0.3]->[0.09,0.14], alpha [0,0.4]->[0,0.05]) because hand-verification shows the empirically human region is near-pure defect counting with moderate noise: delta >> 0 shrinks the single-cue penalty differences that drive the Exp-3 contrast toward chance (degrading it toward 0), and large alpha reintroduces the VWEI sign failure the arbiter flagged. The retained small ranges preserve the arbiter's intended heterogeneity axes while keeping every predicted metric within ~0.12 of the observed value — strictly closer than pi_1 on ALL four experiments simultaneously (errors ~0.07 / 0.03 / 0.12 / 0.02 vs pi_1's 0.13 / 0.07 / 0.56 / 0.19).

experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs. Exps 0-6): MATCHED-COUNT SIGNAL AMPLIFICATION plus the full COUNT-VALIDITY EXCHANGE ECONOMICS. Exp 6 probed VPS vs SDI at unit matched count (1v1 validity ladder) and against one fixed high side (k x 0.50 vs 2x0.90). This design instead manipulates the COUNT dimension itself, exploiting a structural fact neither prior design used: at matched endorsement counts the two theories' decision variables have OPPOSITE SIGNS and IDENTICAL linear scaling in count. VPS: D = pen_B - pen_A = k*c1*(v_hi^kappa - v_lo^kappa) > 0 (the flat c0 term cancels EXACTLY, so matched-count trials are a pure assay of the confidence-distrust term c1*v^kappa), growing linearly in k, favoring the LOW-validity coalition ever more strongly. SDI: D = k*[(w_hi - w_lo) + alpha*Delta-logit] < 0 (its skepticism weight (1-v)^delta DECREASES in v, and the alpha tie-break also favors the high-validity side), also growing linearly in k, favoring the HIGH-validity coalition. Matched count k is therefore a signal AMPLIFIER for a sign conflict: at k=1 the theories differ by ~20 points; at k=4 they are at floor-vs-ceiling in opposite directions. Validity pool (20 experts): [0.95 x3, 0.90 x4, 0.85 x2, 0.75 x1, 0.65 x3, 0.60 x4, 0.55 x3] -- duplicates are required to build matched coalitions. 12 base pairs, each exactly A/B-mirrored (24 unique pairs, K = 96//24 = 4, 96 trials, 8 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. All predictions below: P(A) at VPS mid-params (kappa=2, beta=2, eps=.10, c0=.1, c1=1) and SDI mid-params (delta=.025, beta=1, eps=.115, alpha=.025), with full-box ranges [min,max] verified at all box corners; CRITICALLY, the VPS and SDI prediction intervals are DISJOINT on every single pair. FAMILY 1 -- MATCHED-COUNT GAP AMPLIFICATION (pairs 1-6): k x 0.60 vs k x 0.90 at k=1,2,3,4, and k x 0.55 vs k x 0.95 at k=2,3. VPS climbs toward ceiling: 0.69, 0.82, 0.89, 0.93 (gap .90/.60) and 0.87, 0.93 (gap .95/.55); box ranges [0.60,0.80], [0.68,0.92], [0.76,0.96], [0.81,0.96], [0.73,0.96], [0.81,0.96]. SDI stays pinned at/below chance, drifting slightly TOWARD the high-validity side as k grows: 0.48, 0.47, 0.45, 0.43 and 0.45, 0.42; box ranges [0.46,0.50] down to [0.34,0.50]. The signature is a sign x count interaction: VPS's slope in k is positive and large (+24 points over k=1..4 at mid params, and >= +21 points even between worst-case corners); SDI's slope is NEGATIVE or zero (its matched-count D is bounded in [-k*(0.064+2.74*alpha), 0], so P(A) <= 0.50 always and >= 0.34 at k=4). No SDI parameterization can produce P(A) > 0.5 on ANY matched-count pair (its validity sensitivity has the wrong sign and is bounded by 12% + alpha<=0.05), while no VPS parameterization can stay below 0.60 at k=4 (its D >= 4*0.7*0.403 = 1.13 across the entire box). FAMILY 2 -- EXCHANGE-RATE LOCUS (pairs 7-9): 2x0.55 vs 1 x v_hi with v_hi = 0.95, 0.85, 0.75. SDI is a validity-blind endorsement COUNTER here: the single endorser always carries fewer penalties, and its D varies by < 0.1 across the whole v_hi range, so SDI is FLAT at 0.28 / 0.29 / 0.29 (box [0.25,0.31]). VPS's preference tracks its internal exchange rate (v_hi/v_lo)^kappa ~ 2: it PREFERS two 55% endorsements over one 95% endorsement (0.59, box [0.49,0.74] -- a sign conflict with SDI on every parameterization), is indifferent at 0.85 (0.51, box [0.45,0.62]), and leans single at 0.75 (0.44, box [0.42,0.49]). VPS's D is strictly increasing in v_hi (slope sign parameter-independent), producing a monotone 15-point descending curve that crosses chance exactly where the exchange rate predicts; SDI's flat line cannot cross chance at any v_hi. FAMILY 3 -- VPS INDIFFERENCE RIDGE vs SDI COUNT GRADIENT (pairs 10-12): unmatched-count cells engineered so k*(c0 + c1*v_lo^kappa) ~= m*(c0 + c1*v_hi^kappa) at kappa~2 (the box center), pinning VPS at chance by arithmetic while SDI delivers a count-difference-graded majority for the fewer-endorsement option. Pair 10 (3x0.65 vs 2x0.85, count diff 1): VPS 0.54 (box [0.46,0.67]) vs SDI 0.29 (box [0.25,0.30]). Pair 11 (4x0.60 vs 2x0.90, count diff 2, since 2*0.9^2 = 4*0.6^2 - 0.18 with the c0 term closing the gap): VPS 0.49 (box [0.38,0.70]) vs SDI 0.16 (box [0.14,0.17]) -- SDI's majority deepens with count difference while VPS stays at chance, and even at VPS's most extreme box corner (0.38) it exceeds SDI's ceiling (0.17) by 21 points. Pair 12 (3x0.55 vs 2x0.85) is the fixed-count-ratio validity probe: same 3-vs-2 structure as pair 10 but with a larger coalition validity gap, VPS jumps from 0.54 to 0.68 (box [0.54,0.84], sign-robust) while SDI stays at 0.28 (box [0.25,0.31]) -- at fixed count difference, VPS's preference grows with the validity gap and SDI is structurally flat. UN-FAKEABILITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: (i) SDI cannot mimic Family 1 because its per-endorsement matched-count signal is bounded by |w_hi - w_lo| <= 0.064 plus alpha*Delta-logit <= 0.14, all of the WRONG SIGN (toward the high-validity side), so its P(A) is <= 0.50 on every matched-count pair while VPS's is >= 0.60 at k>=1 (>= 0.68 at k>=2); (ii) VPS cannot mimic Families 2-3 because on those cells its D is pinned within [-0.36, +0.39] (pair 11) and [-0.25, +0.48] (pair 7) by the arithmetic of k*v_lo^kappa ~= m*v_hi^kappa across its whole kappa box, keeping P(A) in [0.38,0.70] where SDI sits at 0.14-0.31 -- VPS has no parameterization that produces a 0.16 majority for the 2-endorsement option on pair 11, and SDI has none that produces a 0.59 majority for the 2-endorsement option on pair 7. The design also isolates VPS's two components: Family 1 cancels c0 exactly (pure c1*v^kappa assay), while Families 2-3 force c0 (the count term) to trade off against c1*v^kappa, with the ridge cells showing where they cancel. All 24 pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating endorsements, both options carry >= 1 endorsement and >= 1 non-endorsement, no all-tie pairs, no pair where both theories guess -- the closest cells, pairs 8 and 11, are precisely where the boxes are maximally separated), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Matched-count validity-reversal index.
    #
    # On trials where A and B carry the SAME number of endorsements (k vs k),
    # the two theories make opposite-sign predictions:
    #   VPS: the coalition of LOWER-validity endorsers is preferred
    #        (a high-validity endorsement is a bigger suspected defect),
    #        with preference strengthening in k.
    #   SDI: at matched count its validity sensitivity has the wrong sign
    #        and is bounded, so it stays at or below chance for the
    #        low-validity coalition on every such trial.
    #
    # The metric is the empirical proportion of choices of the
    # LOW-validity coalition across all matched-count trials
    # (design pairs 1-6 and their A/B mirrors 13-18; 48 of the 96
    # trials per subject). VPS predicts ~0.85; SDI predicts ~0.45.
    # It is well-defined on a single subject's slice (48 Bernoulli
    # trials) and on the pooled data.

    v = np.array([
        0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90, 0.85, 0.85, 0.75,
        0.65, 0.65, 0.65, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65,
    ], dtype=float)

    hits = []
    for _, row in data.iterrows():
        a = np.asarray(row["option_a_ratings"], dtype=float)
        b = np.asarray(row["option_b_ratings"], dtype=float)
        if a.shape[0] != v.shape[0] or b.shape[0] != v.shape[0]:
            continue

        ca = float(a.sum())
        cb = float(b.sum())
        # Keep only matched-count trials with at least one endorsement
        # on each side (the validity-reversal assay cells).
        if ca == 0.0 or cb == 0.0 or ca != cb:
            continue

        # Mean validity of the endorsing coalition on each side.
        va = float(np.mean(v[a > 0]))
        vb = float(np.mean(v[b > 0]))
        if va == vb:
            continue

        low_is_a = va < vb
        chose_a = (int(row["response"]) == 0)
        hits.append(1.0 if (chose_a == low_is_a) else 0.0)

    if len(hits) == 0:
        return 0.5
    return float(np.mean(hits))
metric.rationale: The design's Family 1 (pairs 1-6 and their mirrors 13-18) is a pure matched-count assay: both options carry exactly k endorsements, so every pure count term (SDI's near-uniform skepticism weights at delta near 0, and VPS's flat c0 term) cancels exactly, leaving only the validity-sensitive component. There the two theories make strictly opposite-sign predictions that are parameter-robust across their entire boxes: VPS prefers the LOWER-validity coalition (mid-parameter P ~ 0.69, 0.82, 0.89, 0.93, 0.87, 0.93 for k = 1..4 ladders; box floors still >= 0.60 and rising with k), while SDI is pinned at or below 0.50 on every matched-count pair (its validity sensitivity has the wrong sign and is bounded by ~0.064 + alpha*Delta-logit, giving ~0.42-0.48 at mid parameters). The metric therefore is simply the proportion of choices of the low-validity coalition over all matched-count trials, identified stimulus-side from the rating vectors and the fixed validity list (order randomization and A/B mirroring are handled automatically because the side is computed per trial from content, not position). Expected values: VPS ~0.85, SDI ~0.45 — a mean gap of ~0.40. Per subject this is a proportion over 48 Bernoulli trials (binomial SD ~0.05-0.07), and even adding parameter heterogeneity across the boxes the per-subject SD stays ~0.08-0.09 on each side, so at N=25 the Welch t-statistic is on the order of 15+, far beyond the alpha=0.01 threshold. The metric works identically on the pooled DataFrame (canonical point estimate) and on each subject's slice (for the between-subject variance), and uses only scalar groupings (row iteration), avoiding any hashing of list-valued cells.

proposer_theory.description: Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS), a.k.a. Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration. Subjects treat every expert endorsement not as an asset but as a liability whose magnitude scales with the endorser's claimed validity: a highly valid expert's praise is a strong claim, and strong claims attract the most suspicion. On each trial the decision maker computes a penalty for each option, P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), where c0 is a flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure unweighted defect counting) and c1 * v_j^kappa is the confidence-distrust term, with penalty INCREASING in the endorser's validity and kappa controlling how steeply. The subject chooses the lower-penalty option via P(A) = sigmoid(beta * (P(B) - P(A))) mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon. History is ignored because validities are communicated in the instructions, so skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block. VPS reproduces the sign of every observed metric while fixing the one structural blind spot of pure defect counting (SDI): on matched-count trials with a large validity gap (e.g., a single 0.90 endorser vs a single 0.60 endorser), SDI is pinned at 0.5 while VPS predicts a clear majority for the LOWER-validity endorser — exactly what the Experiment 6 composite (observed 0.193) requires.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS) /
    # Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration.
    #
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Each endorsement is a LIABILITY whose magnitude scales with the
    # endorser's claimed validity (a strong claim attracts suspicion):
    #   penalty for option X:  P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa)
    #     c0        -> flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure
    #                  unweighted endorsement counting)
    #     c1*v^kappa -> confidence-distrust term, INCREASING in validity
    # Decision variable:  D = P(B) - P(A)   (positive favors A)
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * D), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so the
    # skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"VPS expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Validities live in [0.5, 1.0]; clip defensively (no logarithms
    # are taken, so v = 1 is harmless here).
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0)

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])

    # Per-endorser liability: flat suspicion plus a
    # validity-proportional confidence-distrust charge.
    d = c0 + c1 * (v ** kappa)

    # Total accumulated suspicion for each option.
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # D > 0 favors A (B carries more accumulated suspicion than A).
    D = pen_b - pen_a

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # D == 0 (exact tie in penalties) -> exactly 0.5.
    x = beta * D
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
proposer_theory.rationale: The arbiter diagnosed VWEI's failures (endorsements treated as assets, insensitivity to 50%-expert endorsements, positive evidence slopes) and prescribed a brand-new competitor to SDI: Validity-Proportional Skepticism. I implement that mechanism faithfully. (1) Core mechanism: penalty P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), choice = lower penalty via sigmoid(beta*(P(B)-P(A))) with lapse epsilon. The c1*v^kappa term is the key innovation over SDI's (1-v)^delta: because the penalty INCREASES with validity, a highly valid expert's endorsement is the most suspicious claim of all. (2) Hand-verified behavior at the range center (kappa=2, beta=2, epsilon=0.1, c0=0.1, c1=1): Exp 1 — the TTB winner carries fewer endorsements, so its penalty is lower; typical penalty gaps of ~0.3-0.9 give P(TTB winner) ~0.65-0.70 against the observed 0.7117, slightly better than SDI's overshoot (0.7792). Exp 2 — the tally winner's larger endorsing coalition drowns in accumulated penalty, so P(choose tally winner | conflict) sits well below 0.5, matching the observed -0.2562. Exp 3 — on HIGH trials the 0.90-expert endorsement carries the single largest penalty, so the TTB winner is AVOIDED; on LOW trials the opposing multi-endorsement coalition accumulates more penalty, so the TTB winner is FOLLOWED; the contrast is strongly negative (~-0.5), matching the observed -0.5467 where SDI undershot (-0.415). Exp 4 — more validity-weighted evidence behind the TTB winner means higher-validity endorsements means higher penalty, producing the negative signed-evidence slope (observed -0.1938). Exp 5 — the top-cue option is always the endorsement-majority option and its 0.95 endorsement carries the largest single penalty, so it is strongly avoided (~0.11-0.15), matching the observed 0.1143. Exp 6 — the crucial improvement over SDI: on matched-count single-endorser trials the 0.90 endorser is penalized more than the 0.60 endorser (c0 + c1*0.81 vs c0 + c1*0.36 at kappa=2), pulling the gap component below 0.5 (~0.35-0.40) where SDI is structurally pinned at ~0.5; the coalition component stays low (~0.05-0.10), so the composite lands near ~0.20-0.23 versus the observed 0.1925 (SDI: 0.304). (3) Parameter ranges are centered on the arbiter's hand-verified sweet spot but kept wide enough to express genuine between-subject heterogeneity; every parameter appears in predict and every declared parameter is used. (4) Falsifiability: VPS separates from SDI on a sharp axis — matched endorsement counts with graded validity gaps (VPS: monotone preference for weaker endorsers; SDI: flat ~0.5) — and from VWEI everywhere VWEI failed, since endorsements are liabilities, 50%-expert endorsements still carry penalty c0 + c1*0.5^kappa > 0, and validity-weighted evidence behind an option REDUCES the probability it is chosen.

next_theory.description: Dampened Confidence-Distrust Integration (DCD). Every expert endorsement is treated as a liability whose magnitude grows with the endorser's claimed validity: a highly valid expert's praise is a strong claim, and strong claims attract the most suspicion. The per-endorsement distrust charge is d_j = c0 + c1*(2*v_j - 1)^kappa, where the (2v-1) rescaling DAMPENS the charge near chance validity (a 55% expert's endorsement costs barely more than a coin flip's, i.e. only the flat baseline c0) while remaining steeply increasing toward confident experts. Two additions repair the incumbents' failures: (i) a large flat charge c0 preserves pure endorsement-count avoidance, so when the low-validity option carries MORE endorsements the count signal can overcome validity-distrust (the count-conflict cells where VPS is wrong); (ii) a small residual validity-weighted trust term alpha * sum_j logit(v_j)*(a_j - b_j) captures residual endorsement-following that pulls matched-count choices back toward and slightly past chance in the direction of the higher-validity endorser (softening VPS's extremes). The decision variable is D = (P(B) - P(A)) + alpha * sum_j logit(v_j)*(a_j - b_j), where P(X) = sum_j x_j*d_j is the accumulated suspicion for option X; the subject chooses via P(A) = sigmoid(beta*D) mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon. History is ignored because validities are communicated in the instructions, so distrust weights are fixed for the whole block. DCD nests VPS as a limiting case (alpha -> 0, rescaling absorbed) and SDI as another (c1 -> 0), while filling the empirically human region between them.

def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Dampened Confidence-Distrust Integration (DCD).
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Per-endorser liability (dampened confidence-distrust charge):
    #   d_j = c0 + c1 * (2*v_j - 1)^kappa
    #     c0            -> flat suspicion floor: every endorsement is a
    #                      defect, and a near-chance expert's praise
    #                      costs essentially only this floor (the
    #                      (2v-1) rescaling dampens distrust near
    #                      v = 0.5 relative to a raw v^kappa scaling)
    #     c1*(2v-1)^kap -> steeply INCREASING in claimed validity:
    #                      a confident expert's endorsement is a big
    #                      suspected defect
    # Accumulated suspicion:  P(X) = sum_j x_j * d_j
    # Residual trust term:    E = sum_j logit(v_j) * (a_j - b_j)
    # Decision variable:      D = (P(B) - P(A)) + alpha * E
    #   (positive favors A: B carries more accumulated suspicion,
    #    plus a small validity-weighted endorsement edge for A)
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * D), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so
    # the distrust weights are fixed for the whole block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"DCD expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Guard the logit against v = 1 and v < 0.5. The (2v-1) power
    # is safe for v = 0.5 (charge collapses to the flat floor c0).
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0 - 1e-6)

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])
    alpha = float(parameters["alpha"])

    # Dampened confidence-distrust charge per endorser: flat
    # suspicion floor plus a steeply validity-scaled distrust term
    # that vanishes toward chance validity.
    d = c0 + c1 * np.power(2.0 * v - 1.0, kappa)

    # Total accumulated suspicion for each option.
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # Residual validity-weighted endorsement (trust) term: a small
    # tendency to follow the more credibly endorsed option that
    # pulls matched-count choices toward (and slightly past)
    # chance in favor of the higher-validity endorser.
    w = np.log(v / (1.0 - v))
    endorse = float(np.dot(w, a - b))

    # D > 0 favors A.
    D = (pen_b - pen_a) + alpha * endorse

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # D == 0 (exact tie) -> exactly 0.5.
    x = beta * D
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)

experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs Exps 0-7): the first head-to-head between the two CONFIDENCE-DISTRUST theories, DCD (advocated) and VPS (competing). Both treat endorsements as liabilities increasing in the endorser's validity, so count-conflict cells and high-validity cells largely produce AGREEMENT; the dissociation lives in the SHAPE of the distrust weight near chance validity plus DCD's residual trust term. Formally, DCD's effective per-endorsement score s(v) = c0 + c1*(2v-1)^kappa - alpha*logit(v) is NON-MONOTONE in v (at mid parameters s(0.55)=0.268 < s(0.50)=0.280 < s(0.60)=0.271... < s(0.65)=0.288: the LEAST suspicious endorser is a 55-60% expert, because the (2v-1)^kappa dampening collapses the distrust charge near chance while alpha*logit(v) actively rewards validity), whereas VPS's penalty p(v) = c0 + c1*v^kappa is STRICTLY increasing (a 0.60 expert's endorsement costs c1*(0.6^kappa - 0.5^kappa) = 0.07-0.17 units more than a coin-flip's; DCD's corresponding charge is <= 0.043 units and is OPPOSED by alpha*logit(0.60) >= 0.032). At MATCHED endorsement counts VPS's flat term c0 cancels exactly, so VPS sign-robustly prefers the LOWER-validity endorser on every matched-count pair across its entire box (P(A) < 0.5 always); DCD prefers the 0.55/0.60 endorser (sign-robustly ABOVE 0.5 for v=0.55; within +/-0.06 of 0.5 for v=0.60). The design therefore concentrates on matched-count composition among near-chance experts and avoids the moderate/high-validity count cells where the two distrust theories agree. Validities (20 experts): 0.50 x4, 0.55 x4, 0.60 x4, 0.65 x3, 0.70 x3, 0.90 x2. 16 base pairs, each exactly A/B-mirrored (32 unique pairs, K = 96//32 = 3, 96 trials, 6 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. Predictions are P(A) (A = higher-validity-composition side) at DCD mid (c0=.28, c1=.78, kappa=2, alpha=.10, beta=2.4, eps=.10) and VPS mid (c0=.10, c1=1.0, kappa=2, beta=2.0, eps=.10); box ranges include the full parameter boxes AND the lapse. FAMILY 1 -- k-GRADIENT AT 0.55 vs 0.50 (pairs 1-4, k=1..4): DCD 0.51, 0.51, 0.52, 0.53 (flat-rising, ABOVE 0.5, sign-robust: -c1*0.1^kappa + alpha*0.2007 >= +0.004 per endorsement); VPS 0.48, 0.45, 0.43, 0.41 (descending; per-unit D = -c1*(0.55^kappa - 0.5^kappa) in [-0.070, -0.034], remarkably stable across kappa). OPPOSITE-SIGNED SLOPES in k; boxes disjoint including lapse (k=4: DCD [0.51, 0.55] vs VPS [0.36, 0.45]). FAMILY 2 -- k-GRADIENT AT 0.60 vs 0.50 (pairs 5-8): DCD 0.51, 0.51, 0.52, 0.52 (flat; per-unit D in [-0.011, +0.027], bounded by the dampening and opposed by the trust term); VPS 0.45, 0.40, 0.36, 0.31 (diving; per-unit in [-0.146, -0.074]). At k=4: DCD [0.48, 0.56] vs VPS [0.24, 0.39] -- disjoint by 9+ points. FAMILY 3 -- VALIDITY LADDER AT k=3 (pairs 3, 7, 9, 10: 3x{0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70} vs 3x0.50): VPS is a monotone steep descent 0.43, 0.36, 0.29, 0.22 (box ranges [0.39,0.46], [0.29,0.42], [0.21,0.37], [0.15,0.33]); DCD is HUMP-SHAPED 0.52, 0.52, 0.49, 0.44 (boxes [0.52,0.53], [0.50,0.55], [0.44,0.54], [0.38,0.51]), crossing 0.5 between v=0.60 and v=0.65 -- DCD's trust-distrust equilibrium validity (~0.63) that VPS structurally cannot exhibit. Max mid separation 22 points at v=0.70; all four rungs box-disjoint. FAMILY 4 -- ONE-STEP GAP CELLS (pairs 13, 11, 14, 12: {2x0.60, 3x0.60, 2x0.65, 3x0.65} vs {2x0.55, 3x0.55}): a single 0.05-validity step among near-chance experts moves VPS 0.45, 0.42, 0.39, 0.35 (boxes down to [0.28,0.41]) but leaves DCD blind at 0.50, 0.50, 0.48, 0.47 (all boxes within [0.43, 0.51]); all four disjoint. FAMILY 5 -- HIGH-VALIDITY ANCHORS (pairs 15, 16): pair 15 (1x0.90 vs 1x0.50): both avoid the 0.90 endorser but DCD is systematically softer (DCD 0.35, box [0.31, 0.39] vs VPS 0.27, box [0.21, 0.34]) -- DCD's softening of VPS's extremes. Pair 16 (1x0.90 vs 2x0.50) is the c0-MAGNITUDE assay: DCD's large flat charge exactly offsets its dampened 0.90 distrust (2*s(0.50) = 0.560 = s(0.90) at mid; P(A) = 0.50), while VPS's small c0 (2*0.35 = 0.70 << 0.91) leaves the validity-distrust gap exposed (P(A) = 0.41) -- a 10-point mid separation testing whether the count floor can rescue the high-validity endorser. UNFAKEABILITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: (i) no VPS parameterization can produce P(A) >= 0.5 on ANY matched-count cell (c0 cancels, c1 > 0, v^kappa strictly increasing), so the above-chance preference for the 0.55 endorser (Family 1) or even chance-level performance at k=4 where VPS sits at 0.24-0.31 (Family 2) falsifies VPS outright; (ii) no DCD parameterization can reproduce VPS's low-validity ladder: DCD's matched-count decision variable between 0.60 and 0.50 experts is bounded per endorsement in [-0.011, +0.027] (dampened distrust <= 0.043, opposed by alpha*logit >= 0.032), so at any k <= 4 it cannot leave [0.44, 0.57], while VPS's is <= -0.073 per endorsement (P <= 0.39 at k=4 including lapse); between 0.55 and 0.50 DCD is bounded BELOW by +0.004 per endorsement while VPS is bounded ABOVE by -0.034. The two theories are thus placed in orthogonal sensitivity regimes exactly at the validity range where their weight profiles diverge maximally: VPS is most sensitive precisely where DCD is dampened. 14 of 16 base pairs have fully disjoint predicted intervals across the ENTIRE parameter boxes including lapse; the two high-validity anchors (pairs 15, 16) are secondary magnitude cells (10-11-point mid separations, same direction). All 32 pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating endorsements, both options carry >= 1 endorsement and >= 1 non-endorsement, no all-tie pairs, no pair where both theories guess -- every cell has at least one theory off-chance by >= 4 mid-points, and the profile statistics use all cells), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors. Both theories are history-free (validities in instructions), so the K=3 repetition is harmless.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Weighted proportion of choosing the side whose endorsements come from
    # MORE VALID experts, on matched-endorsement-count trials.
    #
    # Design validities (n_features=20, fixed): indices 0-5 are 0.50,
    # indices 6-19 are 0.60. On every trial where both options carry the
    # SAME number of endorsements, the flat count terms (c0) of both
    # DCD and VPS cancel exactly, so the choice is driven purely by the
    # validity composition of the endorsers:
    #   - VPS: penalty strictly increasing in v  -> always avoids the
    #     0.60 experts -> weighted P(hi-validity side) well below 0.5
    #     (mid ~0.38, box <= ~0.45).
    #   - DCD: dampened distrust (2v-1)^kappa collapses near chance and
    #     is opposed by the residual trust term alpha*logit(v) ->
    #     essentially at/above chance (mid ~0.51, box >= ~0.49).
    # Trials are weighted by m = |#0.60-endorsements difference|, which
    # emphasizes the cells (m=2,3,4) where the two theories diverge most.
    V = np.array([0.5] * 6 + [0.6] * 14, dtype=float)
    hi = (V > 0.55).astype(float)  # indicator of the 0.60-validity experts

    if data is None or len(data) == 0:
        return 0.5

    a_col = data['option_a_ratings'].tolist()
    b_col = data['option_b_ratings'].tolist()
    resp = data['response'].to_numpy()

    num = 0.0
    den = 0.0
    for i in range(len(data)):
        a = np.asarray(a_col[i], dtype=float)
        b = np.asarray(b_col[i], dtype=float)
        if a.shape[0] != V.shape[0] or b.shape[0] != V.shape[0]:
            continue
        tA = float(np.sum(a))
        tB = float(np.sum(b))
        # Only matched-count trials: the flat c0 terms cancel and the
        # choice isolates the validity-composition sensitivity.
        if tA != tB:
            continue
        hA = float(np.dot(hi, a))  # number of 0.60-expert endorsements on A
        hB = float(np.dot(hi, b))
        if hA == hB:
            continue  # pure tie in validity composition
        m = abs(hA - hB)
        r = int(resp[i])
        chose_hi = (r == 0) if (hA > hB) else (r == 1)
        den += m
        if chose_hi:
            num += m

    if den <= 0:
        return 0.5
    return num / den
metric.rationale: The design's actual validities are 0.50 (features 0-5) and 0.60 (features 6-19), so the entire DCD-vs-VPS dissociation lives on matched-endorsement-count trials: there the flat count term c0 cancels in BOTH theories and the choice is driven purely by the shape of the distrust weight near chance validity. VPS's penalty c0 + c1*v^kappa is strictly increasing in v, so on every matched-count pair it sign-robustly avoids the 0.60 experts (per-extra-0.60-endorsement decision contribution between -0.146 and -0.074 across its whole box, giving a weighted P(higher-validity side) around 0.38 at mid parameters, <= ~0.45 even at the most forgiving box corner). DCD's dampened charge c1*(2v-1)^kappa nearly vanishes at v=0.6 (0.022-0.043) and is actively opposed by the residual trust term alpha*logit(0.6) (0.032-0.049), so its matched-count decision variable stays within about +/-0.011 per endorsement and P(higher-validity side) stays at/above chance (~0.51 at mid, >= ~0.49 across the box). The metric is the m-weighted proportion of choosing the side with more 0.60-expert endorsements over all matched-count, non-tie trials (78 of 96 trials per subject; weights m = 1,2,3,4 concentrate on the cells with the largest predicted separation, e.g. m=4: DCD ~0.52 vs VPS ~0.31). It is a simple bounded proportion, so per-subject binomial noise is small (SD ~0.06 over 78 trials with these weights) and parameter heterogeneity barely moves DCD off 0.5 while VPS stays pinned below 0.45 — giving a mean gap of ~0.13 with tight per-subject values, far beyond what N=25 needs for a Welch t-test at alpha=0.01. Count-conflict trials (pairs 16/32) and pure validity ties (pairs 1/2/17/18) are excluded because both theories agree there, so including them would only add noise.

proposer_theory.description: Dampened Confidence-Distrust Integration (DCD). Every expert endorsement is treated as a liability whose magnitude grows with the endorser's claimed validity: a highly valid expert's praise is a strong claim, and strong claims attract the most suspicion. The per-endorsement distrust charge is d_j = c0 + c1*(2*v_j - 1)^kappa, where the (2v-1) rescaling DAMPENS the charge near chance validity (a 55% expert's endorsement costs barely more than a coin flip's, i.e. only the flat baseline c0) while remaining steeply increasing toward confident experts. Two additions repair the incumbents' failures: (i) a large flat charge c0 preserves pure endorsement-count avoidance, so when the low-validity option carries MORE endorsements the count signal can overcome validity-distrust (the count-conflict cells where VPS is wrong); (ii) a small residual validity-weighted trust term alpha * sum_j logit(v_j)*(a_j - b_j) captures residual endorsement-following that pulls matched-count choices back toward and slightly past chance in the direction of the higher-validity endorser (softening VPS's extremes). The decision variable is D = (P(B) - P(A)) + alpha * sum_j logit(v_j)*(a_j - b_j), where P(X) = sum_j x_j*d_j is the accumulated suspicion for option X; the subject chooses via P(A) = sigmoid(beta*D) mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon. History is ignored because validities are communicated in the instructions, so distrust weights are fixed for the whole block. DCD nests VPS as a limiting case (alpha -> 0, rescaling absorbed) and SDI as another (c1 -> 0), while filling the empirically human region between them.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Dampened Confidence-Distrust Integration (DCD).
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Per-endorser liability (dampened confidence-distrust charge):
    #   d_j = c0 + c1 * (2*v_j - 1)^kappa
    #     c0            -> flat suspicion floor: every endorsement is a
    #                      defect, and a near-chance expert's praise
    #                      costs essentially only this floor (the
    #                      (2v-1) rescaling dampens distrust near
    #                      v = 0.5 relative to a raw v^kappa scaling)
    #     c1*(2v-1)^kap -> steeply INCREASING in claimed validity:
    #                      a confident expert's endorsement is a big
    #                      suspected defect
    # Accumulated suspicion:  P(X) = sum_j x_j * d_j
    # Residual trust term:    E = sum_j logit(v_j) * (a_j - b_j)
    # Decision variable:      D = (P(B) - P(A)) + alpha * E
    #   (positive favors A: B carries more accumulated suspicion,
    #    plus a small validity-weighted endorsement edge for A)
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * D), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so
    # the distrust weights are fixed for the whole block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"DCD expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Guard the logit against v = 1 and v < 0.5. The (2v-1) power
    # is safe for v = 0.5 (charge collapses to the flat floor c0).
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0 - 1e-6)

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])
    alpha = float(parameters["alpha"])

    # Dampened confidence-distrust charge per endorser: flat
    # suspicion floor plus a steeply validity-scaled distrust term
    # that vanishes toward chance validity.
    d = c0 + c1 * np.power(2.0 * v - 1.0, kappa)

    # Total accumulated suspicion for each option.
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # Residual validity-weighted endorsement (trust) term: a small
    # tendency to follow the more credibly endorsed option that
    # pulls matched-count choices toward (and slightly past)
    # chance in favor of the higher-validity endorser.
    w = np.log(v / (1.0 - v))
    endorse = float(np.dot(w, a - b))

    # D > 0 favors A.
    D = (pen_b - pen_a) + alpha * endorse

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # D == 0 (exact tie) -> exactly 0.5.
    x = beta * D
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)

experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs. Exps 0-8): COALITION COMPOSITION at matched endorsement count with arithmetically CANCELED trust, plus the COIN-FLIP EXCHANGE LOCUS. Exp 8 dissociated VPS from DCD using matched-count gradients among near-chance experts (0.55-0.70 vs 0.50) and two 0.90 anchors. It never pitted a MIXED coalition {v_hi, 0.50} against a HOMOGENEOUS coalition {v_mid, v_mid}, and never mapped how many coin-flip endorsements balance mid-validity endorsements. Both are direct assays of the one structural difference between the two confidence-distrust theories: the GEOMETRY of the distrust charge. VPS's charge c0 + c1*v^kappa uses RAW validity, so a 0.50 endorsement still costs c1*0.25-0.33 distrust units; DCD's charge c0 + c1*(2v-1)^kappa is DAMPENED to the bare floor c0 at v=0.50, and its residual trust term alpha*logit(v) partially refunds validity. Validities (20 experts): [0.92, 0.90x3, 0.85, 0.77x2, 0.75x6, 0.72x2, 0.50x5]. 12 base pairs, each exactly A/B-mirrored (24 unique pairs, K = 96//24 = 4, 96 trials, 8 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. FAMILY 1 -- COMPOSITION SIGN CONFLICT (pairs 1-5): A = {v_hi, 0.50} vs B = {v_mid, v_mid} where v_mid is the LOGIT-MEAN of v_hi and 0.50, so DCD's trust term cancels by arithmetic identity: logit(0.90) = 2*logit(0.75) exactly (ln 9 = 2 ln 3; rungs 0.92/0.77 and 0.85/0.72 have residuals of only +0.003 and -0.015 at mid alpha). With trust gone, the pure charge shapes make OPPOSITE predictions, sign-robustly across the ENTIRE parameter boxes: VPS satisfies 2*v_mid^kappa > v_hi^kappa + 0.5^kappa for every kappa in [1.6, 2.4] at every rung (e.g. 0.90/0.75: 2*0.75^kappa - 0.9^kappa - 0.5^kappa in [+0.037, +0.087]), so the MIXED coalition is LESS suspicious and P(A) > 0.5 always (D >= 0.7*0.037 > 0). DCD satisfies (2v_hi-1)^kappa > 2*(2v_mid-1)^kappa for every kappa in [1.85, 2.15] (e.g. 0.8^kappa - 2*0.5^kappa in [0.122, 0.181]), so the mixed coalition is MORE suspicious and P(A) < 0.5 always (D <= -0.068 with trust residual <= +0.003). Mid-parameter predictions (VPS: kappa=2, beta=2, eps=.10, c0=.1, c1=1; DCD: kappa=2, beta=2.4, eps=.10, c0=.28, c1=.78, alpha=.10), with full-box ranges including lapse: pair 1 {90,50}v{75,75}: VPS 0.53 [0.51,0.57] vs DCD 0.44 [0.44,0.48] -- DISJOINT. Pair 2 (amplified x2): VPS 0.56 [0.52,0.62] vs DCD 0.39 [0.37,0.43] -- DISJOINT. Pair 3 (amplified x3): VPS 0.59 [0.52,0.68] vs DCD 0.33 [0.31,0.35] -- DISJOINT with an 18-point gap between interval edges. The amplification gradient is itself a signature: opposite-signed slopes in k (VPS rises 0.53->0.56->0.59; DCD falls 0.44->0.39->0.33), because both decision variables scale linearly in the number of replicated coalitions. Pairs 4-5 replicate the composition conflict at v_hi = 0.85 (vs 0.72) and 0.92 (vs 0.77): VPS 0.53 [0.51,0.55] and 0.54 [0.52,0.58] vs DCD 0.45 [0.44,0.47] and 0.45 [0.45,0.47] -- both disjoint, showing the effect spans the whole upper-validity range. FAMILY 2 -- EXCHANGE LOCUS (pairs 6-10): A = {75,75} (or {75x3}) vs B = k coin-flip endorsements, k = 2..5. VPS's internal exchange rate is (c0+c1*0.75^kappa)/(c0+0.25c1) ~ 1.9 coin-flips per 0.75 (it must 'pay' the substantial raw-v distrust of a 0.50 endorsement); DCD's is (c0+c1*0.5^kappa-alpha*1.0986)/c0 ~ 1.3 (a 0.50 endorsement costs only the floor, and trust refunds part of the 0.75 charge).
