The indifference point therefore differs by a full rung: VPS crosses 50% between k=3 and k=4 per two 0.75s; DCD crosses between k=2 and k=3. Pair 6 (k=2): VPS 0.25 [0.22,0.35] vs DCD 0.41 [0.38,0.48] -- disjoint magnitude conflict. Pair 7 (k=3): SIGN CONFLICT, VPS 0.38 [0.26,0.48] vs DCD 0.56 [0.48,0.64]. Pair 8 (k=4): VPS 0.53 [0.41,0.67] vs DCD 0.70 [0.60,0.76] -- DCD robustly prefers TWO 0.75 endorsements over FOUR coin-flips; VPS calls it near-chance. Pair 9 (k=5): agreement baseline (VPS 0.68, DCD 0.80). Pair 10 ({75x3} vs {50x5}, ratio 1.67 -- squarely between the two exchange rates): the strongest cell in the design, SIGN CONFLICT with VPS 0.40 [0.26,0.55] vs DCD 0.66 [0.53,0.71]; DCD's D > 0 by >= 0.076 at every box corner while VPS's mid D = -0.24. FAMILY 3 -- CALIBRATION (pairs 11-12): pair 11 ({90} vs {50}) both avoid the 0.90 endorser with DCD systematically softer (VPS 0.27 [0.20,0.34] vs DCD 0.35 [0.32,0.45]); pair 12 ({50,50} vs {90,90}) is a ceiling agreement cell (VPS 0.86, DCD 0.76) that scales each theory's slope where they concur. UNFAKEABILITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: (i) on all five composition cells, no DCD parameterization can reach P(A) = 0.5 (its D is negative by >= 0.068 with the trust residual bounded in [-0.019, +0.003]), and no VPS parameterization can fall to 0.5 (its D is positive by >= 0.026) -- the sign of the majority choice on any composition cell adjudicates the theories with no free parameters able to reverse it, and the k-amplification makes the P3 cell a 26-point mid separation; (ii) on the exchange family, the only VPS corner that reaches a positive decision variable on pair 10 (c0=0.15, c1=0.7, kappa=2.4) simultaneously predicts pair 6 at 0.34 (vs DCD 0.43) and pair 3 at 0.53 (vs DCD 0.31) -- a joint profile across cells that neither theory's box can mimic, since the composition conflict and the exchange conflict are two faces of the same structural difference (raw-v vs dampened charge) and no single reparameterization flips both. As the VPS advocate, the predicted profile is: majority for the MIXED coalition on all composition cells, growing with amplification (0.53 -> 0.59), and coin-flip avoidance that persists through k=3 (0.38) with an indifference point near k=4. A DCD subject instead shows majority-HOMOGENEOUS on all composition cells (falling to 0.33 at k=3), near-chance already at k=3 on the exchange gradient (0.56), and a robust preference for two 0.75s over four coin-flips (0.70). All 24 pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating endorsements, both options carry >= 1 endorsement and >= 1 non-endorsement, no all-tie pairs, no pair where both theories guess), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors. Both theories are history-free (validities in the instructions), so K=4 repetition is harmless.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # COIN-FLIP ENDORSEMENT TOLERANCE.
    #
    # For every trial, count how many endorsements each option receives
    # from the five chance-validity (v = 0.50) experts (feature indices
    # 15-19 in this experiment's fixed validity vector). Every one of the
    # 24 unique pairs pits an option carrying coin-flip endorsements
    # against an option carrying none, so the trial is scored:
    #   1.0  if the subject chose the option with MORE 0.50-expert
    #        endorsements (the 'coin-flip tolerant' choice),
    #   0.0  otherwise.
    # The metric is the mean of this score over all trials.
    #
    # This is a direct assay of the one structural difference between the
    # two confidence-distrust theories: the geometry of the per-endorsement
    # distrust charge. VPS charges c0 + c1*v^kappa, so a 0.50 endorsement
    # still costs a substantial c1*0.25-0.33 distrust units and the
    # internal exchange rate between mid-validity (0.75) endorsements and
    # coin-flips is ~1.9 coin-flips per 0.75. DCD charges
    # c0 + c1*(2v-1)^kappa, which collapses to the bare floor c0 at
    # v = 0.50 (and refunds part of the 0.75 charge via the residual trust
    # term), yielding an exchange rate of only ~1.3. Hence VPS subjects
    # are systematically MORE willing to accept coin-flip endorsements,
    # across every cell family in the design:
    #   composition cells (mixed {v_hi, 0.50} vs homogeneous mid): VPS
    #     picks the mixed side (0.53-0.59), DCD avoids it (0.33-0.45);
    #   exchange cells (0.75-coalition vs k coin-flips): VPS keeps
    #     choosing the coin-flip side through k=3-4, DCD abandons it;
    #   calibration cells ({0.90} vs {0.50}, {0.50,0.50} vs {0.90,0.90}):
    #     VPS 0.73/0.86 vs DCD 0.65/0.76.
    # Mid-parameter predictions: VPS ~0.59, DCD ~0.45 (disjoint across
    # their full parameter boxes), with per-subject SD ~0.05-0.06 from
    # 96 Bernoulli trials.

    validities = np.array([
        0.92, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90, 0.85, 0.77, 0.77,
        0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 0.72, 0.72,
        0.50, 0.50, 0.50, 0.50, 0.50,
    ])
    coin_mask = np.isclose(validities, 0.5)

    responses = data["response"].to_numpy()
    ratings_a = data["option_a_ratings"].tolist()
    ratings_b = data["option_b_ratings"].tolist()

    scores = []
    for i in range(len(ratings_a)):
        a = np.asarray(ratings_a[i], dtype=float).ravel()
        b = np.asarray(ratings_b[i], dtype=float).ravel()
        n = min(a.shape[0], b.shape[0], validities.shape[0])
        mask = coin_mask[:n]
        ca = float(np.sum(a[:n][mask]))
        cb = float(np.sum(b[:n][mask]))
        if ca == cb:
            # No coin-flip asymmetry on this trial; skip defensively.
            continue
        chose_a = (int(responses[i]) == 0)
        c_chosen = ca if chose_a else cb
        c_other = cb if chose_a else ca
        scores.append(1.0 if c_chosen > c_other else 0.0)

    if len(scores) == 0:
        return 0.5
    return float(np.mean(scores))
metric.rationale: The metric is the proportion of trials on which the subject chose the option carrying MORE endorsements from the five v=0.50 (coin-flip) experts. Every one of the 24 unique pairs (96 trials/subject, 4 reps each) has a strict coin-flip asymmetry, so all trials contribute, and the metric is a simple Bernoulli proportion that works identically on the pooled data and on a single subject's 96-trial slice. It targets the single structural difference between the theories: VPS's raw-v charge c0+c1*v^kappa makes a 0.50 endorsement cost substantial distrust (exchange rate ~1.9 coin-flips per 0.75 endorsement), while DCD's dampened charge c0+c1*(2v-1)^kappa collapses to the floor c0 at v=0.50 with a trust refund (exchange rate ~1.3). Consequently, on every cell family the VPS subject is more coin-flip tolerant: composition cells (mixed {v_hi,0.50} vs homogeneous mid-validity) give VPS 0.53/0.56/0.59 (pairs 1-3, amplified) vs DCD 0.44/0.39/0.33 — opposite-signed majorities that no parameterization in either box can reverse; exchange cells (75-coalition vs k coin-flips) give VPS 0.75/0.62/0.47/0.32/0.60 vs DCD 0.59/0.44/0.30/0.20/0.34; calibration cells give VPS 0.73/0.86 vs DCD 0.65/0.76. Averaging over all 24 pairs: VPS mid-parameter value ≈ 0.59, DCD ≈ 0.45 — a 0.146 mean gap that is disjoint across the two theories' full parameter boxes (VPS per-cell box ranges stay above DCD's on essentially every cell, with the composition cells sign-robust). Per-subject standard deviation is ~0.05 (binomial over 96 trials) plus modest parameter heterogeneity (~0.02-0.04), giving Welch t ≈ 8-9 at N=25, far below alpha=0.01. Averaging over all cells (rather than only the sign-conflict cells) maximizes the standardized gap because the added trials shrink the binomial variance faster than the moderate cells dilute the mean difference, and it makes the metric a single interpretable behavioral quantity — coin-flip endorsement tolerance — rather than a hand-picked subset of trials.

proposer_theory.description: Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS), a.k.a. Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration. Subjects treat every expert endorsement not as an asset but as a liability whose magnitude scales with the endorser's claimed validity: a highly valid expert's praise is a strong claim, and strong claims attract the most suspicion. On each trial the decision maker computes a penalty for each option, P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), where c0 is a flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure unweighted defect counting) and c1 * v_j^kappa is the confidence-distrust term, with penalty INCREASING in the endorser's validity and kappa controlling how steeply. The subject chooses the lower-penalty option via P(A) = sigmoid(beta * (P(B) - P(A))) mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon. History is ignored because validities are communicated in the instructions, so skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block. VPS reproduces the sign of every observed metric while fixing the one structural blind spot of pure defect counting (SDI): on matched-count trials with a large validity gap (e.g., a single 0.90 endorser vs a single 0.60 endorser), SDI is pinned at 0.5 while VPS predicts a clear majority for the LOWER-validity endorser — exactly what the Experiment 6 composite (observed 0.193) requires.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS) /
    # Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration.
    #
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Each endorsement is a LIABILITY whose magnitude scales with the
    # endorser's claimed validity (a strong claim attracts suspicion):
    #   penalty for option X:  P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa)
    #     c0        -> flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure
    #                  unweighted endorsement counting)
    #     c1*v^kappa -> confidence-distrust term, INCREASING in validity
    # Decision variable:  D = P(B) - P(A)   (positive favors A)
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * D), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so the
    # skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"VPS expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Validities live in [0.5, 1.0]; clip defensively (no logarithms
    # are taken, so v = 1 is harmless here).
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0)

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])

    # Per-endorser liability: flat suspicion plus a
    # validity-proportional confidence-distrust charge.
    d = c0 + c1 * (v ** kappa)

    # Total accumulated suspicion for each option.
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # D > 0 favors A (B carries more accumulated suspicion than A).
    D = pen_b - pen_a

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # D == 0 (exact tie in penalties) -> exactly 0.5.
    x = beta * D
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
proposer_theory.rationale: The arbiter diagnosed VWEI's failures (endorsements treated as assets, insensitivity to 50%-expert endorsements, positive evidence slopes) and prescribed a brand-new competitor to SDI: Validity-Proportional Skepticism. I implement that mechanism faithfully. (1) Core mechanism: penalty P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), choice = lower penalty via sigmoid(beta*(P(B)-P(A))) with lapse epsilon. The c1*v^kappa term is the key innovation over SDI's (1-v)^delta: because the penalty INCREASES with validity, a highly valid expert's endorsement is the most suspicious claim of all. (2) Hand-verified behavior at the range center (kappa=2, beta=2, epsilon=0.1, c0=0.1, c1=1): Exp 1 — the TTB winner carries fewer endorsements, so its penalty is lower; typical penalty gaps of ~0.3-0.9 give P(TTB winner) ~0.65-0.70 against the observed 0.7117, slightly better than SDI's overshoot (0.7792). Exp 2 — the tally winner's larger endorsing coalition drowns in accumulated penalty, so P(choose tally winner | conflict) sits well below 0.5, matching the observed -0.2562. Exp 3 — on HIGH trials the 0.90-expert endorsement carries the single largest penalty, so the TTB winner is AVOIDED; on LOW trials the opposing multi-endorsement coalition accumulates more penalty, so the TTB winner is FOLLOWED; the contrast is strongly negative (~-0.5), matching the observed -0.5467 where SDI undershot (-0.415). Exp 4 — more validity-weighted evidence behind the TTB winner means higher-validity endorsements means higher penalty, producing the negative signed-evidence slope (observed -0.1938). Exp 5 — the top-cue option is always the endorsement-majority option and its 0.95 endorsement carries the largest single penalty, so it is strongly avoided (~0.11-0.15), matching the observed 0.1143. Exp 6 — the crucial improvement over SDI: on matched-count single-endorser trials the 0.90 endorser is penalized more than the 0.60 endorser (c0 + c1*0.81 vs c0 + c1*0.36 at kappa=2), pulling the gap component below 0.5 (~0.35-0.40) where SDI is structurally pinned at ~0.5; the coalition component stays low (~0.05-0.10), so the composite lands near ~0.20-0.23 versus the observed 0.1925 (SDI: 0.304). (3) Parameter ranges are centered on the arbiter's hand-verified sweet spot but kept wide enough to express genuine between-subject heterogeneity; every parameter appears in predict and every declared parameter is used. (4) Falsifiability: VPS separates from SDI on a sharp axis — matched endorsement counts with graded validity gaps (VPS: monotone preference for weaker endorsers; SDI: flat ~0.5) — and from VWEI everywhere VWEI failed, since endorsements are liabilities, 50%-expert endorsements still carry penalty c0 + c1*0.5^kappa > 0, and validity-weighted evidence behind an option REDUCES the probability it is chosen.

next_theory.description: Softened Validity-Distrust with Count Mixture (SVD). Every expert endorsement is a liability whose magnitude increases monotonically in the endorser's RAW claimed validity: d_j = c0 + c1*v_j^kappa, with no dampening near v=0.5 and no trust refund. Decision making is a dual-process mixture at the trial level: with probability w the subject is a 'skeptic' who integrates the accumulated-suspicion difference D = P(B) - P(A) through sigmoid(beta*D); with probability (1-w) the subject is a 'counter' who simply chooses the option with FEWER total endorsements (indifferent at matched counts). Two heterogeneity mechanisms soften the pooled extremes and capture between-subject variability: (i) the sigmoid slope beta is sampled from a WIDE per-subject range, so the population is a mixture of shallow and steep sigmoids — sensitive near D=0 (matched-count validity-composition trials) yet compressed at large |D| (unequal-count trials); (ii) the uniform lapse epsilon is also sampled from a wide per-subject range, which pulls every saturated large-D assay toward 0.5 while adding genuine between-subject dispersion in overall choice rates.
next_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Softened Validity-Distrust with Count Mixture (SVD).
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Branch 1 (skeptic, prob w): each endorsement is a LIABILITY whose
    # magnitude grows with the endorser's RAW claimed validity:
    #   d_j = c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa   (kappa >= 1.5; NO dampening near
    #                                v = 0.5, NO trust refund)
    #   accumulated suspicion: P(X) = sum_j x_j * d_j
    #   D = P(B) - P(A)  (positive favors A)
    #   P_skeptic(A) = sigmoid(beta * D)
    # Branch 2 (counter, prob 1-w): pure tallying on endorsement COUNTS;
    #   choose the option with FEWER total endorsements; exactly
    #   indifferent (0.5) at matched counts.
    # Mixture: P_core(A) = w * P_skeptic(A) + (1-w) * P_count(A),
    # mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so the
    # distrust weights are fixed for the whole block. beta AND epsilon
    # are sampled per subject from WIDE ranges: between-subject
    # heterogeneity in the sigmoid slope and in the lapse rate are
    # explicit parts of the theory.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SVD expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0)  # defensive; no logs taken, v=1 harmless.

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])
    w_mix = float(parameters["w"])

    # --- Skeptic branch: raw validity-proportional distrust charge ---
    d = c0 + c1 * np.power(v, kappa)
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # D > 0 favors A (B carries more accumulated suspicion).
    D = pen_b - pen_a
    x = beta * D
    p_skeptic_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))  # stable sigmoid

    # --- Counter branch: pure endorsement-count tallying ---
    cnt_a = float(np.sum(a))
    cnt_b = float(np.sum(b))
    if cnt_a < cnt_b:
        p_count_a = 1.0      # A has fewer endorsements -> prefer A
    elif cnt_a > cnt_b:
        p_count_a = 0.0
    else:
        p_count_a = 0.5      # matched counts -> indifferent

    # --- Dual-process mixture ---
    p_a = w_mix * p_skeptic_a + (1.0 - w_mix) * p_count_a
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
next_theory.rationale: This is a parameter-box-only minimal-diff edit of the ACCEPTED iter-5 base (loss 0.0481): predict/policy are re-emitted verbatim and only two ranges move, exactly per the critic's iter-5 diagnosis. (1) PRIMARY KNOB — epsilon raised and widened from [0.10, 0.16] to [0.12, 0.24] (mean ~0.18, inside the arbiter's 0.10-0.25 sketch). The iter-5 decomposition showed every remaining residual lives on the saturated large-D / unequal-count assays (Exp 1 +0.077, Exp 10 +0.031, Exp 4 -0.027, Exp 2 -0.026), where beta heterogeneity has no leverage because both mixture branches are pinned (the counter branch votes deterministically for the TTB winner on Exp 1's conflict trials and the skeptic's sigmoid is saturated for most of the beta range). The lapse is the only in-family knob that pulls saturated rates toward 0.5: it moves Exp 1 from 0.789 toward ~0.74-0.75, Exp 10 toward ~0.52, Exp 4 toward -0.20, Exp 2 toward -0.26, and even Exp 5 (rate 0.095, target 0.114) in the correct direction, at a small ~0.01-0.02 cost on the well-calibrated matched-count assays (6, 7, 8, 9). The wide per-subject spread also directly attacks the systematic 3-10x underprediction of between-subject variance on every experiment, which a narrow epsilon box cannot. (2) MICRO-KNOB — w ceiling raised from 0.90 to 0.92 only. The critic explicitly corrected the iter-4 guardrail's sign error: lowering w would shift weight onto the counter branch's deterministic 1.0 on Exp 1's conflict trials and RAISE Exp 1 further; raising w slightly shifts weight onto the skeptic branch (which sits below 1.0 there), mildly lowering Exp 1 and Exp 10 while sharpening the matched-count assays (Exp 8 up toward 0.78, Exp 9 down toward 0.37), partially offsetting the epsilon costs. The move is capped at +0.02 per the critic's instruction. (3) FROZEN — beta stays at the wide [1.2, 2.6] box that just closed Exps 7 and 8 (re-narrowing it would undo the loop's biggest win); c0, c1, kappa stay at the validated iter-3/5 charge geometry that produces correct signs and near-correct magnitudes on every validity-composition assay. Guardrails respected: if Exp 8 falls below ~0.75 or Exp 6 rises above ~0.24, the retreat is the epsilon ceiling (to ~0.19), not beta or w; if Exp 2 drifts below -0.30, back w off rather than epsilon. Architecture, mechanism family, and all function code are untouched.

experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs. Exps 0-9): the first head-to-head between SVD (advocated) and VPS (competing) -- two theories that share the SAME distrust core. SVD's skeptic branch is functionally identical to VPS (penalty c0 + c1*v^kappa per endorsement, D = pen_B - pen_A, sigmoid(beta*D), uniform lapse), and SVD's parameter box is essentially NESTED inside VPS's (c0 [0.05,0.12] within [0.05,0.15]; c1 [0.95,1.3] within [0.7,1.3]; kappa [1.5,1.8] within [1.6,2.4] up to a 0.1 sliver). Two consequences drive the design. (1) A box-robust SIGN conflict is provably impossible: any penalty difference that is decisively signed across VPS's box is also signed on the shared region of SVD's box, so both cores always point the same way. The dissociation must therefore be QUANTITATIVE -- in CHANGES across cells and in saturation LEVELS. (2) Everything that distinguishes the theories flows from SVD's counter mixture (probability 1-w in [0.08,0.20]: a deterministic fewer-endorsement tally that is EXACTLY indifferent at matched counts) plus SVD's wider lapse. The design's keystone is a manipulation that is orthogonal to everything VPS computes: COUNT PARITY at fixed, saturated penalty evidence. Validities (20 experts): 0.95 x7, 0.75 x4, 0.50 x9. 12 base pairs, each exactly A/B-mirrored (24 unique pairs, K = 96//24 = 4, 96 trials, 8 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. Mid parameters used below: SVD (c0=.085, c1=1.125, kappa=1.65, beta=1.9, w=.86, eps=.18); VPS (c0=.10, c1=1.0, kappa=2, beta=2, eps=.10); box ranges verified at box corners. FAMILY 1 -- SATURATED COUNT-PARITY JUMP (pairs 1-4, primary): pair 1 is A = {50x7} vs B = {95x7}, a matched-count cell with a huge penalty gap (D = 7*c1*(0.95^k - 0.5^k) >= 2.90 on VPS's box, >= 3.81 on SVD's). Pair 2 adds ONE coin-flip endorsement to B (counts 7v8); pair 3 adds ONE coin-flip to A (8v7); pair 4 adds TWO to A (9v7). The added endorsements are 0.50 experts, whose penalty contribution (0.18-0.58 units) is trivial against the saturated D (3-6 units), so VPS's decision variable is essentially untouched: VPS's predicted P(A) is FLAT across all four pairs -- box-verified changes: Delta(pair2 - pair1) in [0, +0.06] points, Delta(pair3 - pair1) in [-0.7, 0], Delta(pair4 - pair1) in [-1.9, 0] -- while its LEVEL on pair 1 is [0.927, 0.965] (worst corner c1=.7, kappa=1.6, beta=1.6, eps=.13 still gives 0.927). SVD behaves completely differently: on pair 1 (matched counts) its counter branch contributes exactly 0.5, capping P(A) at (1-eps)(1+w)/2 + eps/2 <= 0.905 (box [0.798, 0.905], mid 0.853) -- DISJOINT from VPS's [0.927, 0.965]; the moment counts become unmatched, the counter branch flips to a deterministic vote: pair 2 (counter favors A) JUMPS to [0.876, 0.940] (mid 0.910), i.e., Delta in [+3.3, +8.8] points; pair 3 (counter favors B) DROPS to [0.717, 0.869] (mid 0.795), Delta in [-8.0, -3.5]; pair 4 drops further to [0.708, 0.869], Delta in [-8.9, -4.4]. THE CHANGES ARE BOX-DISJOINT: VPS moves at most 1.9 points where SVD moves at least 3.3 (pair 2) and at least 3.5 (pairs 3-4). A count-parity effect of >= 2 points at saturation falsifies VPS outright (no beta, kappa, c0, c1, or epsilon in its box can produce it); a flat profile (changes <= 2 points) falsifies SVD outright. The pair-1 LEVEL alone is nearly decisive: P(A) >= 0.92 falsifies SVD; <= 0.91 falsifies VPS. SVD additionally predicts the counter branch is a STEP at parity, not a gradient: pairs 3 and 4 are predicted nearly equal (mid 0.795 both). FAMILY 2 -- MATCHED-COUNT CEILING LADDER (pairs 10-12 + pair 1): k x 0.50 vs k x {0.75 or 0.95} at k = 2, 2, 4, 7. Both theories prefer the coin-flip side, but VPS climbs to its ceiling (mid: 0.750, 0.889, 0.945, 0.950; box at k=7: [0.927, 0.965]) while SVD is compressed toward 0.5 by the factor (1-eps)*w ~ 0.65 and plateaus (mid: 0.702, 0.803, 0.849, 0.853; box at k=7: [0.798, 0.905]). The asymptote LEVEL (>= 0.92 vs <= 0.91) and the ~10-point mid gap at every saturated rung is the signature; SVD's between-subject dispersion on the asymptote (wide eps in [0.12,0.24] and w in [0.80,0.92]) is a secondary heterogeneity signature VPS cannot produce (its eps box [0.07,0.13] spans 3 points of asymptote, SVD's spans 11). FAMILY 3 -- COUNTER BUFFERING ON CONFLICT CELLS (pairs 5-7): A = {95 x j} vs B = {50 x 2j}, j = 1, 2, 3. Here the skeptic core of BOTH theories prefers B (the coin-flip side: 2 coin-flips cost less suspicion than one 0.95 endorsement, sign-robustly: VPS's D = j*[c0 + c1*(2*0.5^k - 0.95^k)] < 0 at every box corner), but SVD's counter branch votes for A (fewer endorsements), dragging SVD back toward chance. VPS dives: mid P(A) = 0.368, 0.256, 0.176 (boxes [0.21,0.49], [0.09,0.48], [0.05,0.47]) -- a deepening B-majority, B-rate 0.63 -> 0.74 -> 0.82 at mid. SVD hovers: mid P(A) = 0.481, 0.411, 0.352 (boxes [0.44,0.51], [0.35,0.49], [0.30,0.47]) -- near chance at j=1 and never below 0.30. A B-rate >= 0.60 on pair 5 falsifies SVD; a B-rate <= 0.52 falsifies VPS; at j=3 the mid separation is 17.6 points. FAMILY 4 -- EXCHANGE-RIDGE CELLS (pairs 8-9): A = {75 x 2} vs B = {50 x 4}, and its x2 amplification A = {75 x 4} vs B = {50 x 8}. These sit exactly at the coin-flip/0.75 exchange ridge where VPS's penalty difference is pinned near zero (VPS mid D = +0.075 and +0.15, P(A) = 0.533 and 0.567; box [0.42,0.69] and [0.33,0.81] -- near chance), because 4 coin-flips cost roughly 2 x 0.75 in suspicion. SVD's exchange rate is slightly lower AND its counter branch votes for the 2-endorsement (or 4-vs-8) side, so SVD delivers a clear A-majority: mid 0.634 and 0.687 (boxes [0.59,0.72], [0.60,0.84]). SVD's P(A) rises with the amplification (+5 mid points, robust: SVD's D > 0 at every box corner since c0 + c1*(2*0.5^k - 0.75^k) >= 0.034 > 0 for kappa in [1.5,1.8], so doubling the coalition strictly increases its skeptic probability while the counter vote stays fixed). UNFAKEABILITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (joint profile): because the boxes are nested, single-cell mimicry is possible only at extreme corners, but the corners that let VPS imitate SVD on one family force it away on the others. The VPS corner that comes closest to SVD on Family 3 (c0=.15, c1=.7, kappa=1.6, the flattest corner, P(A)=0.489 on pair 5) simultaneously predicts P(A) = 0.927 on pair 1 with a count-jump of ~0 -- while SVD's box requires P(A) <= 0.905 AND a jump >= +3.3; conversely, the SVD corner that maximizes pair 1 (eps=.12, w=.92: 0.905, jump +3.5) predicts pair 5 at 0.51, far above VPS's ceiling there (0.49), and pair 7 at 0.47 vs VPS's 0.47 only at its flattest corner where pair 1 sits at 0.93. The conjunction {pair-1 level, count-jump size, Family-3 depth, ladder asymptote} is a profile neither box can approximate: VPS is a flat line at 0.93-0.97 across Family 1 with deep B-majorities in Family 3; SVD is a V-shaped step function on Family 1 (0.85 -> 0.91 -> 0.80 -> 0.80 at mid) with near-chance performance in Family 3 and an 0.85 asymptote. All 24 pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating endorsements, both options carry >= 1 endorsement and >= 11 non-endorsements, no all-tie pairs, and no pair leaves both theories guessing -- the closest cells, pairs 5 and 8, are exactly where the boxes maximally separate at mid), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors. Both theories are history-free (validities in the instructions), so K=4 repetition is harmless.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Saturated-conflict compliance rate.
    #
    # Logic: using a FIXED reference parameterization of the shared skeptic
    # core (c0=0.10, c1=1.0, kappa=2.0 -> d_j = 0.10 + v_j^2), compute the
    # skeptic decision variable D = pen(B) - pen(A) for every trial, plus the
    # raw endorsement counts cnt_A, cnt_B.
    #
    # Keep only trials that are (i) SATURATED for the skeptic core
    # (|D| > 2.0, so any plausible beta in either theory's box drives the
    # sigmoid to ~1) and (ii) in CONFLICT: the skeptic-preferred side is the
    # side with MORE endorsements (the pure counter branch votes the other
    # way). In this fixed design these are exactly the count-parity-jump
    # cells pairs 3, 4 and their mirrors 15, 16 (16 trials per subject).
    #
    # On these cells the two theories make disjoint predictions:
    #   VPS:  P(pick skeptic side) = (1-eps)*~1 + eps/2  ~ 0.95 (box 0.92-0.98)
    #   SVD:  P = (1-eps)*(w*1 + (1-w)*0) + eps/2 = (1-eps)*w + eps/2
    #         ~ 0.80 (box 0.73-0.87, since the counter mixture drags the
    #         saturated response toward the fewer-endorsement side).
    # The metric is the observed fraction of choices that follow the
    # skeptic-preferred side on these cells.

    validities = [0.95] * 7 + [0.75] * 4 + [0.50] * 9
    d_ref = [0.10 + 1.0 * (v ** 2) for v in validities]

    hits = []
    for _, row in data.iterrows():
        a_raw = row["option_a_ratings"]
        b_raw = row["option_b_ratings"]
        a = [int(float(x)) for x in a_raw]
        b = [int(float(x)) for x in b_raw]

        pen_a = sum(di for di, xi in zip(d_ref, a) if xi == 1)
        pen_b = sum(di for di, xi in zip(d_ref, b) if xi == 1)
        D = pen_b - pen_a  # >0 favors A

        cnt_a = sum(1 for x in a if x == 1)
        cnt_b = sum(1 for x in b if x == 1)

        # (i) saturation for the skeptic core
        if abs(D) <= 2.0:
            continue
        # counter branch must be decisive (not indifferent)
        if cnt_a == cnt_b:
            continue

        skeptic_prefers_a = D > 0
        counter_prefers_a = cnt_a < cnt_b  # fewer endorsements preferred

        # (ii) conflict: counter branch votes AGAINST the saturated skeptic core
        if skeptic_prefers_a == counter_prefers_a:
            continue

        resp = int(row["response"])  # 0 = chose A, 1 = chose B
        followed_skeptic = (resp == 0) if skeptic_prefers_a else (resp == 1)
        hits.append(1.0 if followed_skeptic else 0.0)

    if len(hits) == 0:
        return 0.5
    return float(np.mean(hits))
metric.rationale:
TARGETED CONTRAST: saturated conflict cells. The design's Family-1 count-parity cells 3, 4 (and mirrors 15, 16) are the one place where the two theories' boxes make DISJOINT LEVEL predictions, not just different change scores. On these trials the shared skeptic core is saturated (|D| ~ 3.9-4.2, so sigmoid(beta*D) ~ 1 for every beta in either theory's box) and it favors the side with MORE endorsements, while SVD's counter branch (prob 1-w) deterministically votes for the FEWER-endorsement side. Hence: VPS predicts P(follow skeptic) = (1-eps)*1 + eps/2 ≈ 0.95 (box 0.92-0.98, tight because VPS's eps box is narrow), whereas SVD predicts P = (1-eps)*w + eps/2 ≈ 0.80 (box 0.73-0.87). Mid gap ≈ 15.5 points, and even the extreme corners of the two boxes do not overlap (SVD max 0.87 < VPS min ~0.92).

WHY THIS METRIC HAS LOW BETWEEN-SUBJECT VARIANCE: (a) Each subject contributes 16 trials of exactly this cell type (4 unique pairs x 4 reps), so the binomial component of per-subject variance is only ~p(1-p)/16 (sd ~ 0.10). (b) The cell is saturated, so SVD's wide beta range [1.2, 2.6] contributes almost nothing (even the weakest corner gives sigmoid ~ 0.99). (c) The remaining heterogeneity (eps in [0.12,0.24], w in [0.80,0.92]) moves the SVD per-subject value only over ~[0.73, 0.87] (sd ~ 0.03), far less than the 15-point mean gap. VPS's per-subject spread is even tighter (~0.05 sd).

EXPECTED NUMBERS: SVD point estimate ~ 0.79-0.80 with between-subject variance ~ 0.011; VPS ~ 0.95 with variance ~ 0.003. Welch's t at N=25: t ≈ 0.155 / sqrt((0.011+0.003)/25) ≈ 6.5, p << 0.001, comfortably below alpha = 0.01.

ROBUSTNESS OF CELL IDENTIFICATION: cells are selected by a generic rule (reference-weighted |D| > 2.0, count mismatch, sign(D) opposite to the fewer-endorsement side) rather than by hardcoded trial indices; with this design's fixed validities and pairs, the rule selects exactly pairs 3, 4, 15, 16 — the next-largest conflicting |D| in the whole design is 0.91 (pair 19), and all other large-|D| cells are either count-matched (counter indifferent: pairs 1, 12, 13, 24) or counter-agreeing (pairs 2, 14), so the selection is unambiguous. The metric works identically on the pooled DataFrame and on a single subject's slice (each slice contains all 96 trials including the 16 target trials).

proposer_theory.description: Softened Validity-Distrust with Count Mixture (SVD). Every expert endorsement is a liability whose magnitude increases monotonically in the endorser's RAW claimed validity: d_j = c0 + c1*v_j^kappa, with no dampening near v=0.5 and no trust refund. Decision making is a dual-process mixture at the trial level: with probability w the subject is a 'skeptic' who integrates the accumulated-suspicion difference D = P(B) - P(A) through sigmoid(beta*D); with probability (1-w) the subject is a 'counter' who simply chooses the option with FEWER total endorsements (indifferent at matched counts). Two heterogeneity mechanisms soften the pooled extremes and capture between-subject variability: (i) the sigmoid slope beta is sampled from a WIDE per-subject range, so the population is a mixture of shallow and steep sigmoids — sensitive near D=0 (matched-count validity-composition trials) yet compressed at large |D| (unequal-count trials); (ii) the uniform lapse epsilon is also sampled from a wide per-subject range, which pulls every saturated large-D assay toward 0.5 while adding genuine between-subject dispersion in overall choice rates.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Softened Validity-Distrust with Count Mixture (SVD).
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Branch 1 (skeptic, prob w): each endorsement is a LIABILITY whose
    # magnitude grows with the endorser's RAW claimed validity:
    #   d_j = c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa   (kappa >= 1.5; NO dampening near
    #                                v = 0.5, NO trust refund)
    #   accumulated suspicion: P(X) = sum_j x_j * d_j
    #   D = P(B) - P(A)  (positive favors A)
    #   P_skeptic(A) = sigmoid(beta * D)
    # Branch 2 (counter, prob 1-w): pure tallying on endorsement COUNTS;
    #   choose the option with FEWER total endorsements; exactly
    #   indifferent (0.5) at matched counts.
    # Mixture: P_core(A) = w * P_skeptic(A) + (1-w) * P_count(A),
    # mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so the
    # distrust weights are fixed for the whole block. beta AND epsilon
    # are sampled per subject from WIDE ranges: between-subject
    # heterogeneity in the sigmoid slope and in the lapse rate are
    # explicit parts of the theory.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SVD expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0)  # defensive; no logs taken, v=1 harmless.

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])
    w_mix = float(parameters["w"])

    # --- Skeptic branch: raw validity-proportional distrust charge ---
    d = c0 + c1 * np.power(v, kappa)
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # D > 0 favors A (B carries more accumulated suspicion).
    D = pen_b - pen_a
    x = beta * D
    p_skeptic_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))  # stable sigmoid

    # --- Counter branch: pure endorsement-count tallying ---
    cnt_a = float(np.sum(a))
    cnt_b = float(np.sum(b))
    if cnt_a < cnt_b:
        p_count_a = 1.0      # A has fewer endorsements -> prefer A
    elif cnt_a > cnt_b:
        p_count_a = 0.0
    else:
        p_count_a = 0.5      # matched counts -> indifferent

    # --- Dual-process mixture ---
    p_a = w_mix * p_skeptic_a + (1.0 - w_mix) * p_count_a
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
proposer_theory.rationale: This is a parameter-box-only minimal-diff edit of the ACCEPTED iter-5 base (loss 0.0481): predict/policy are re-emitted verbatim and only two ranges move, exactly per the critic's iter-5 diagnosis. (1) PRIMARY KNOB — epsilon raised and widened from [0.10, 0.16] to [0.12, 0.24] (mean ~0.18, inside the arbiter's 0.10-0.25 sketch). The iter-5 decomposition showed every remaining residual lives on the saturated large-D / unequal-count assays (Exp 1 +0.077, Exp 10 +0.031, Exp 4 -0.027, Exp 2 -0.026), where beta heterogeneity has no leverage because both mixture branches are pinned (the counter branch votes deterministically for the TTB winner on Exp 1's conflict trials and the skeptic's sigmoid is saturated for most of the beta range). The lapse is the only in-family knob that pulls saturated rates toward 0.5: it moves Exp 1 from 0.789 toward ~0.74-0.75, Exp 10 toward ~0.52, Exp 4 toward -0.20, Exp 2 toward -0.26, and even Exp 5 (rate 0.095, target 0.114) in the correct direction, at a small ~0.01-0.02 cost on the well-calibrated matched-count assays (6, 7, 8, 9). The wide per-subject spread also directly attacks the systematic 3-10x underprediction of between-subject variance on every experiment, which a narrow epsilon box cannot. (2) MICRO-KNOB — w ceiling raised from 0.90 to 0.92 only. The critic explicitly corrected the iter-4 guardrail's sign error: lowering w would shift weight onto the counter branch's deterministic 1.0 on Exp 1's conflict trials and RAISE Exp 1 further; raising w slightly shifts weight onto the skeptic branch (which sits below 1.0 there), mildly lowering Exp 1 and Exp 10 while sharpening the matched-count assays (Exp 8 up toward 0.78, Exp 9 down toward 0.37), partially offsetting the epsilon costs. The move is capped at +0.02 per the critic's instruction. (3) FROZEN — beta stays at the wide [1.2, 2.6] box that just closed Exps 7 and 8 (re-narrowing it would undo the loop's biggest win); c0, c1, kappa stay at the validated iter-3/5 charge geometry that produces correct signs and near-correct magnitudes on every validity-composition assay. Guardrails respected: if Exp 8 falls below ~0.75 or Exp 6 rises above ~0.24, the retreat is the epsilon ceiling (to ~0.19), not beta or w; if Exp 2 drifts below -0.30, back w off rather than epsilon. Architecture, mechanism family, and all function code are untouched.

experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs. Exps 0-10): PERFECT EXPERTS (v = 1.0) combined with MINIMAL COUNT ASYMMETRY (+/-1, +/-2 endorsements). Exp 10, the only prior SVD-vs-VPS design, used 0.95/0.75/0.50 experts and 2:1 count ratios; its conflict cells left VPS's weak box corners unsaturated (its Family-3 VPS intervals reached up to [0.05, 0.47]), so VPS could mimic SVD's levels at extreme corners. The v = 1.0 expert closes that escape route STRUCTURALLY: its distrust charge is c0 + c1*1^kappa = c0 + c1 -- the maximum possible and KAPPA-INVARIANT -- so no parameterization of either theory can discount it, while the coin-flip expert's charge c0 + c1*0.5^kappa (in [0.18, 0.58] on VPS's box) is the cheapest suspicion unit; the charge ratio (c0+c1)/(c0+c1*0.5^kappa) is >= 2.23 at every VPS corner. On a 6-perfect-vs-7-coin cell VPS's decision variable is D = c0 + c1*(7*0.5^kappa - 6) <= -2.43 at EVERY corner of its box: VPS is pinned at its floor (or ceiling) by arithmetic, not by favorable parameters. Meanwhile a SINGLE extra coin-flip endorsement -- worth at most 0.58 penalty units against a 2-6 unit saturated gap -- flips SVD's deterministic counter branch from voting one way, to indifferent, to voting the other way. Validities (15 experts): 1.0 x 6, 0.50 x 9. 12 base stimuli, each exactly A/B-mirrored (24 unique pairs, K = 96//24 = 4, 96 trials, 8 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. Mid parameters quoted: VPS (kappa=2, beta=2, eps=.10, c0=.10, c1=1.0; charges: perfect 1.10, coin 0.35); SVD (c0=.085, c1=1.125, kappa=1.65, beta=1.9, w=.86, eps=.18; charges: perfect 1.21, coin 0.443); box ranges verified at box corners. FAMILY 1 -- SATURATED FLOOR (pairs 1-3): A carries j perfect endorsements (j=4,6) vs B's j+1 (pair 3: j+2) coin-flips. VPS: P(A) in [0.050, 0.138] (pair 1), [0.050, 0.082] (pair 2), [0.050, 0.096] (pair 3) -- near-certain avoidance of the perfect-expert side at every corner. SVD: its skeptic branch is equally saturated toward B, but its counter branch (prob 1-w >= 0.08) deterministically votes A (fewer endorsements): P(A) = (1-eps)(w*s + (1-w)) + eps/2 >= 0.130 on all three (boxes [0.130, 0.294], [0.130, 0.285], [0.130, 0.293]; mid 0.210, 0.205, 0.205). DISJOINT on pairs 2-3 (VPS max 0.082/0.096 < SVD min 0.130); pair 1 is a near-disjoint gradient rung (15.6 mid points, 8-point box overlap). An A-rate >= 0.12 on pairs 2-3 falsifies VPS outright; <= 0.11 falsifies SVD outright. This floor-level pinning is what Exp 10's 0.95-expert cells could not achieve. FAMILY 2 -- SATURATED CEILING, COUNTER-OPPOSED (pairs 14-15, mirrors of 2-3): A = 7 (or 8) coin endorsements vs B = 6 perfect. Both cores saturate toward A; SVD's counter votes B. VPS: P(A) >= 0.919 (pair 14), >= 0.904 (pair 15), up to 0.951. SVD: P(A) = (1-eps)*w*s + eps/2 <= 0.870 (boxes [0.715, 0.870], [0.710, 0.870]; mid 0.795 both). DISJOINT: an A-rate >= 0.91 falsifies SVD; <= 0.88 falsifies VPS. Unlike Exp 10's matched-count ceiling cells (SVD cap 0.905), the counter branch here actively drags SVD 3-8 points further from VPS. FAMILY 3 -- THE COUNT-PARITY STAIRCASE (pairs 2 -> 4 -> 5 floor side; 14 -> 16 -> 17 ceiling side): the perfect-expert side's endorsement count climbs 6 -> 7 -> 8 (one added coin-flip expert per rung) against a FIXED 7-coin opponent, so the skeptic evidence stays saturated (|D| >= 2.05 at every corner of both boxes) while count parity passes through fewer -> matched -> more. SVD is a STAIRCASE: mid P(A) = 0.205 -> 0.147 -> 0.090 (floor side) and 0.795 -> 0.853 -> 0.910 (ceiling side), with a step of exactly (1-w)(1-eps)/2 in [3.0, 8.8] points at EVERY parity crossing -- the step size is a direct read on SVD's mixture and lapse parameters. VPS is FLAT: a coin endorsement shifts D by at most 0.58 units against |D| >= 2.05, so P(A) moves <= 0.7 points box-wide (floor side [0.050,0.082] -> [0.050,0.075] -> [0.050,0.071]; ceiling side [0.919,0.951] -> [0.926,0.951] -> [0.929,0.951]). The change intervals are DISJOINT at every step (SVD >= 3.0 points where VPS <= 0.7). Any single coin-flip endorsement moving choice by >= 2 points on these saturated cells falsifies VPS (no beta, kappa, c0, c1, or epsilon in its box can produce it); flatness (<= 2 points) falsifies SVD outright. Pair 4's LEVEL is additionally disjoint by itself: VPS [0.050, 0.075] vs SVD [0.150, 0.156] -- SVD's matched-count indifference cap (1-eps)(1+w)/2 + eps/2 keeps it 7.5+ points above VPS's floor even though its skeptic branch, like VPS's, is fully saturated. FAMILY 4 -- THE EXCHANGE LOCUS (pairs 7-10): one perfect endorsement vs m = 1, 2, 3, 4 coin-flips. VPS mid: 0.214, 0.329, 0.478, 0.631 -- crossing 50% between m=3 and m=4 (internal exchange rate (c0+c1)/(c0+c1*0.5^kappa) = 3.14 at mid, in [2.23, 4.56] across the box). SVD mid: 0.280, 0.452, 0.598, 0.730 -- crossing between m=2 and m=3 (skeptic rate 2.73 at mid, in [2.59, 2.88], PLUS the counter branch voting for the single-endorsement side at m >= 2, pulling the crossing a full rung earlier). SIGN CONFLICT at m=3 (pair 8): VPS 0.478 (slight B-majority) vs SVD 0.598 (clear A-majority), 12 mid points; at m=2 (pair 7) VPS is at a clear B-majority (0.329) where SVD sits near chance (0.452). Boxes overlap here (VPS's exchange-rate range is wide), so this family is a SECONDARY crossing-rung signature: the observed indifference rung is m=3-4 for VPS vs m=2-3 for SVD, and the joint profile adjudicates corner ambiguity -- the VPS corner that crosses earliest (c0=0.15, c1=0.7, kappa=1.6, giving P(pair 8) = 0.598) is still pinned flat on the staircase and <= 0.138 on every floor cell, so a subject showing SVD's crossing rung TOGETHER WITH any staircase step >= 2 points or any floor-cell A-rate >= 0.12 lies outside VPS's entire box. FAMILY 5 -- MIXED-COALITION EXCHANGE (pairs 11-12): two perfect endorsements vs 5 (then 6) coin-flips: VPS 0.310, 0.455 vs SVD 0.489, 0.636 -- 18-point mid gaps in the same direction (SVD's counter votes the 2-endorsement side), secondary magnitude cells. FAMILY 6 -- MATCHED-COUNT CEILING BASELINE (pairs 6, 18): 6 perfect vs 6 coin, counts matched. VPS [0.926, 0.951] vs SVD [0.841, 0.905] (pair 6; mirror flipped) -- disjoint; the v=1.0 sharpening of Exp 10's pair-1 level assay (VPS's matched-count D = 6*c1*(1-0.5^kappa) >= 2.81 across its box). UNFAKEABILITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: (i) No VPS parameterization can produce the staircase: on staircase cells |D| >= 2.05 at every VPS corner while a coin endorsement is worth <= 0.58 units, bounding VPS's per-rung change at 0.7 points vs SVD's structural step (1-w)(1-eps)/2 >= 3.0. (ii) No VPS parameterization can reach SVD's floor levels on pairs 2-3 (box max 0.082/0.096 < SVD box min 0.130) or pair 4 (0.075 < 0.150). (iii) No SVD parameterization can reach VPS's ceiling on pairs 14-15 (counter-opposed cap (1-eps)w + eps/2 <= 0.870 < VPS min 0.904) or the matched-count cells 6/16/18 (indifference cap <= 0.905 < VPS min 0.926). (iv) The parameters trade off oppositely: SVD's most VPS-like corner (eps=0.12, w=0.92) simultaneously gives floor cells at 0.130 (still 3.4+ points above VPS's pairs-2/3 ceiling of 0.096), ceiling cells at 0.870 (still below VPS's 0.904 floor), and staircase steps of 3.5 points (still 2.8 points above VPS's 0.7 maximum) -- every SVD corner is disjoint from every VPS corner on at least two families, and the conjunction {floor level, ceiling level, staircase step, exchange crossing} is a profile neither box can approximate: a VPS subject is a flat line at 0.05/0.95 across the staircase with a 3-4-rung exchange crossing; an SVD subject is a 0.13-0.29 floor, a 0.71-0.87 counter-opposed ceiling, a 3-9-point staircase whose step size estimates (1-w)(1-eps)/2, and a 2-3-rung exchange crossing. All 24 pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating endorsements, both options carry >= 1 endorsement and >= 7 non-endorsements, no all-tie pairs, and no pair leaves both theories guessing -- the closest cells, pairs 5 and 17, are exactly the staircase rungs where the step signature lives), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors. Both theories are history-free (validities in the instructions), so K=4 repetition is harmless.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # COIN-SIDE CHOICE RATE ON SATURATED PERFECT-VS-COIN CELLS.
    #
    # Features 0..5 are the validity-1.0 ("perfect") experts; features
    # 6..14 are the coin-flip (v=0.5) experts.
    #
    # Selected cells: one option carries >= 4 perfect endorsements with
    # <= 7 total endorsements, the other carries 0 perfect and >= 5 coin
    # endorsements. This selects exactly the 10 saturated pairs
    # (1,2,3,4,6 and their A/B mirrors 13,14,15,16,18), i.e. 40 of the
    # 96 trials per subject. The staircase top rung (pairs 5/17) and the
    # exchange-locus pairs are deliberately excluded: there the two
    # theories overlap or the per-subject spread is maximal.
    #
    # The metric is the rate of CHOOSING THE COIN-ONLY SIDE (i.e. avoiding
    # the perfect-endorser side), pooled over floor trials and their
    # mirrors, which cancels any side bias.

    n_perf = 6
    df = data.reset_index(drop=True)

    hits = []
    for a_raw, b_raw, resp in zip(
        df["option_a_ratings"], df["option_b_ratings"], df["response"]
    ):
        a = [int(x) for x in a_raw]
        b = [int(x) for x in b_raw]

        perfA = sum([1 for i in range(len(a)) if a[i] == 1 and i < n_perf])
        coinA = sum([1 for i in range(len(a)) if a[i] == 1 and i >= n_perf])
        perfB = sum([1 for i in range(len(b)) if b[i] == 1 and i < n_perf])
        coinB = sum([1 for i in range(len(b)) if b[i] == 1 and i >= n_perf])

        a_heavy = (perfA >= 4) and ((perfA + coinA) <= 7)
        b_heavy = (perfB >= 4) and ((perfB + coinB) <= 7)
        a_coin = (perfA == 0) and (coinA >= 5)
        b_coin = (perfB == 0) and (coinB >= 5)

        if a_heavy and b_coin:
            # A is the perfect-heavy side, so the coin-only side is B.
            hits.append(1.0 if int(resp) == 1 else 0.0)
        elif b_heavy and a_coin:
            # B is the perfect-heavy side, so the coin-only side is A.
            hits.append(1.0 if int(resp) == 0 else 0.0)

    if len(hits) == 0:
        return 0.5
    return float(np.mean(hits))
metric.rationale:
My previous submission of this metric never reached the statistical evaluation: it died on a SyntaxError at compile time (almost certainly a non-ASCII character in the docstring interacting badly with the harness's exec path), so the underlying contrast was never tested. This is the corrected, pure-ASCII implementation of the same assay, with the sign flipped to the more natural VPS framing (rate of AVOIDING the perfect endorser) and list comprehensions used everywhere per the guardrails.

Why this contrast is the right one at N=25: the level of the saturated cells is a LEVEL assay (a plain mean of binary indicators over 40 fixed trials), not a difference/slope assay, so its per-subject variance is essentially binomial plus parameter heterogeneity, with no differencing noise. On the selected cells the perfect expert's distrust charge is c0 + c1*1^kappa = c0 + c1, the maximum possible and kappa-invariant, so VPS's decision variable is <= -2.4 at every corner of its box: VPS's coin-side rate is pinned at 1 - eps/2, i.e. in [0.935, 0.965] (mean ~0.95), with per-subject sd dominated by binomial noise over 40 trials (~0.034) plus a tiny eps heterogeneity contribution (~0.008). SVD's skeptic branch is equally saturated toward the coin side, but its counter branch (probability 1-w in [0.08, 0.20]) votes by raw endorsement count: FOR the perfect side on pairs 1-3 (fewer endorsements) and INDIFFERENT on the matched-count pairs 4/6, giving a coin-side rate of (1-eps)*w + eps/2 on pairs 1-3 and (1-eps)*(1+w)/2 + eps/2 on pairs 4/6. Across SVD's whole box this ranges from ~0.73 to ~0.88 (mid ~0.80-0.85 per pair, mid-parameter mean ~0.82), with per-subject sd ~0.07 (binomial ~0.06 plus w/eps heterogeneity ~0.035, in quadrature). Expected Welch t at N=25: (0.95 - 0.82) / sqrt((0.0013 + 0.0050)/25) ~= 8-9, far below alpha = 0.01, and the gap stays positive (>= 0.05) even at the two most mutually-favorable parameter corners (VPS eps=0.13 vs SVD eps=0.12, w=0.92), so the test is robust to wherever in the boxes the simulator places the parameters. Design choices that tighten the test: (i) pooling floor pairs with their A/B mirrors makes the metric a pure 'avoid the perfect endorser' rate, cancelling side bias; (ii) excluding the staircase top rung (pairs 5/17), where SVD's counter also votes the coin side and its coin-side rate (1 - eps/2 in [0.88, 0.94]) overlaps VPS's, removes the one diluting cell type; (iii) excluding the exchange-locus pairs (near 0.5, maximal binomial variance, overlapping boxes) removes pure noise; (iv) the metric is a simple mean of indicators, well defined on the pooled DataFrame and on each single subject's 96-trial slice, so the between-subject variance is always available. The metric is not trivially true for VPS: it pins VPS at its lapse ceiling by arithmetic (the kappa-invariant charge of a v=1.0 expert), and any human subject avoiding the perfect-endorser side on <= 88% of these trials falsifies VPS outright while matching SVD's counter-branch signature.

proposer_theory.description: Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS), a.k.a. Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration. Subjects treat every expert endorsement not as an asset but as a liability whose magnitude scales with the endorser's claimed validity: a highly valid expert's praise is a strong claim, and strong claims attract the most suspicion. On each trial the decision maker computes a penalty for each option, P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), where c0 is a flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure unweighted defect counting) and c1 * v_j^kappa is the confidence-distrust term, with penalty INCREASING in the endorser's validity and kappa controlling how steeply. The subject chooses the lower-penalty option via P(A) = sigmoid(beta * (P(B) - P(A))) mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon. History is ignored because validities are communicated in the instructions, so skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block. VPS reproduces the sign of every observed metric while fixing the one structural blind spot of pure defect counting (SDI): on matched-count trials with a large validity gap (e.g., a single 0.90 endorser vs a single 0.60 endorser), SDI is pinned at 0.5 while VPS predicts a clear majority for the LOWER-validity endorser — exactly what the Experiment 6 composite (observed 0.193) requires.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Validity-Proportional Skepticism (VPS) /
    # Confidence-Distrust Defect Integration.
    #
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # Each endorsement is a LIABILITY whose magnitude scales with the
    # endorser's claimed validity (a strong claim attracts suspicion):
    #   penalty for option X:  P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa)
    #     c0        -> flat defect-count term (c1 = 0 recovers pure
    #                  unweighted endorsement counting)
    #     c1*v^kappa -> confidence-distrust term, INCREASING in validity
    # Decision variable:  D = P(B) - P(A)   (positive favors A)
    # P(A) = sigmoid(beta * D), mixed with a uniform lapse epsilon.
    # History is ignored: validities are in the instructions, so the
    # skepticism weights are fixed for the whole block.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"VPS expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Validities live in [0.5, 1.0]; clip defensively (no logarithms
    # are taken, so v = 1 is harmless here).
    v = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0)

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])

    # Per-endorser liability: flat suspicion plus a
    # validity-proportional confidence-distrust charge.
    d = c0 + c1 * (v ** kappa)

    # Total accumulated suspicion for each option.
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # D > 0 favors A (B carries more accumulated suspicion than A).
    D = pen_b - pen_a

    # Numerically stable sigmoid: 0.5 * (1 + tanh(x/2)).
    # D == 0 (exact tie in penalties) -> exactly 0.5.
    x = beta * D
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * x))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
proposer_theory.rationale: The arbiter diagnosed VWEI's failures (endorsements treated as assets, insensitivity to 50%-expert endorsements, positive evidence slopes) and prescribed a brand-new competitor to SDI: Validity-Proportional Skepticism. I implement that mechanism faithfully. (1) Core mechanism: penalty P(X) = sum_j x_j * (c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa), choice = lower penalty via sigmoid(beta*(P(B)-P(A))) with lapse epsilon. The c1*v^kappa term is the key innovation over SDI's (1-v)^delta: because the penalty INCREASES with validity, a highly valid expert's endorsement is the most suspicious claim of all. (2) Hand-verified behavior at the range center (kappa=2, beta=2, epsilon=0.1, c0=0.1, c1=1): Exp 1 — the TTB winner carries fewer endorsements, so its penalty is lower; typical penalty gaps of ~0.3-0.9 give P(TTB winner) ~0.65-0.70 against the observed 0.7117, slightly better than SDI's overshoot (0.7792). Exp 2 — the tally winner's larger endorsing coalition drowns in accumulated penalty, so P(choose tally winner | conflict) sits well below 0.5, matching the observed -0.2562. Exp 3 — on HIGH trials the 0.90-expert endorsement carries the single largest penalty, so the TTB winner is AVOIDED; on LOW trials the opposing multi-endorsement coalition accumulates more penalty, so the TTB winner is FOLLOWED; the contrast is strongly negative (~-0.5), matching the observed -0.5467 where SDI undershot (-0.415). Exp 4 — more validity-weighted evidence behind the TTB winner means higher-validity endorsements means higher penalty, producing the negative signed-evidence slope (observed -0.1938). Exp 5 — the top-cue option is always the endorsement-majority option and its 0.95 endorsement carries the largest single penalty, so it is strongly avoided (~0.11-0.15), matching the observed 0.1143. Exp 6 — the crucial improvement over SDI: on matched-count single-endorser trials the 0.90 endorser is penalized more than the 0.60 endorser (c0 + c1*0.81 vs c0 + c1*0.36 at kappa=2), pulling the gap component below 0.5 (~0.35-0.40) where SDI is structurally pinned at ~0.5; the coalition component stays low (~0.05-0.10), so the composite lands near ~0.20-0.23 versus the observed 0.1925 (SDI: 0.304). (3) Parameter ranges are centered on the arbiter's hand-verified sweet spot but kept wide enough to express genuine between-subject heterogeneity; every parameter appears in predict and every declared parameter is used. (4) Falsifiability: VPS separates from SDI on a sharp axis — matched endorsement counts with graded validity gaps (VPS: monotone preference for weaker endorsers; SDI: flat ~0.5) — and from VWEI everywhere VWEI failed, since endorsements are liabilities, 50%-expert endorsements still carry penalty c0 + c1*0.5^kappa > 0, and validity-weighted evidence behind an option REDUCES the probability it is chosen.

next_theory.description: Graded Dual-Route Distrust with a Bimodal Strategy Population (GDRD-B). Subjects evaluate expert endorsements through two concurrent routes. ROUTE 1 (analytic distrust): every endorsement is a liability whose magnitude grows monotonically in the endorser's RAW claimed validity, d_j = c0 + c1*v_j^kappa; accumulated suspicion P(X) = sum_j x_j*d_j is compared across options through sigmoid(beta*(P(B)-P(A))), plus a small residual micro-trust edge alpha*sum_j clip(logit(v_j),0,3)*(a_j-b_j) (capped so perfect experts exert bounded, not unbounded, trust pull). ROUTE 2 (graded counting): a continuous preference for the fewer-endorsement option, sigmoid(gamma*(cnt_B-cnt_A)). The population is BIMODAL in the route weight w: a large majority (~88%) of 'skeptics' (w in [0.85, 0.95], moderate lapse) coexists with a minority (~12%) of 'counters' (w in [0.50, 0.62], low lapse, decisive count slope gamma >= 2). The mixture is implemented as a quantile transform of a single uniform per-subject population variable u_pop, which holds the population-MEAN route weight at its base value while exploding the between-subject behavioral variance — the empirically observed 3-12x super-binomial variance on the saturation assays (Exps 11, 12) that no uniform range-widening could reproduce.
next_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Graded Dual-Route Distrust, bimodal-population variant (GDRD-B).
    #
    # Stimulus: array-like of shape (2, n_features), row 0 = option A,
    # row 1 = option B; entries are binary expert ratings.
    #
    # ROUTE 1 (analytic distrust, weight w): each endorsement is a
    # LIABILITY whose magnitude grows with the endorser's RAW claimed
    # validity:
    #   d_j = c0 + c1 * v_j^kappa          (kappa >= 1, no dampening
    #                                        near v = 0.5)
    #   accumulated suspicion: P(X) = sum_j x_j * d_j
    #   D = (P(B) - P(A)) + alpha * sum_j clip(logit(v_j), 0, 3)*(a_j - b_j)
    #     (micro-trust term; the logit is CAPPED at 3 so perfect
    #      experts exert bounded, not unbounded, trust pull)
    #   P_skeptic(A) = sigmoid(beta * D)
    # ROUTE 2 (graded counting, weight 1-w): a CONTINUOUS preference
    # for the option with fewer total endorsements:
    #   P_count(A) = sigmoid(gamma * (cnt_B - cnt_A))
    #
    # BIMODAL POPULATION: instead of sampling w, gamma, epsilon from
    # independent uniform ranges (which shifts the population MEANS
    # whenever the ranges widen), a single uniform population quantile
    # u_pop in [0, 1] is deterministically mapped onto a two-component
    # mixture:
    #   u_pop < 0.12  -> 'counter' minority:  w in [0.50, 0.62],
    #                    epsilon in [0.05, 0.10], gamma in [2.0, 3.0]
    #   otherwise     -> 'skeptic' majority:   w in [0.85, 0.95],
    #                    epsilon in [0.08, 0.18], gamma in [1.5, 3.0]
    # This holds E[w] at the calibrated base value (~0.86) while
    # producing genuine between-subject bimodality — the mechanism the
    # real super-binomial variances on Exps 11/12 demand.
    #
    # History is ignored: validities are communicated in the
    # instructions, so the distrust weights are fixed for the whole
    # block. beta is sampled per subject from a wide range.
    if isinstance(state, dict):
        a_vec = np.asarray(state["option_a_ratings"], dtype=float).ravel()
        b_vec = np.asarray(state["option_b_ratings"], dtype=float).ravel()
        stim = np.vstack([a_vec, b_vec])
    else:
        stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"GDRD expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )
    # Power route: v = 1 is harmless (no logs). Trust route: guard
    # the logit against v = 1 (perfect experts) and v < 0.5.
    v_pow = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0)
    v_tr = np.clip(v, 0.5, 1.0 - 1e-6)

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    c0 = float(parameters["c0"])
    c1 = float(parameters["c1"])
    alpha = float(parameters["alpha"])
    u_pop = float(parameters["u_pop"])

    # --- Bimodal population mixture over (w, epsilon, gamma) ---
    # Quantile transform of one uniform variable: the population mean
    # route weight stays at the calibrated base (~0.86) while the
    # between-subject distribution becomes bimodal.
    f_counter = 0.12
    u = min(max(u_pop, 0.0), 1.0)
    if u < f_counter:
        # Counter minority: near-balanced routes, low lapse, decisive
        # graded count slope.
        t = u / f_counter
        w_mix = 0.50 + 0.12 * t          # [0.50, 0.62]
        epsilon = 0.05 + 0.05 * t        # [0.05, 0.10]
        gamma = 2.0 + 1.0 * t            # [2.0, 3.0]
    else:
        # Skeptic majority: analytic-distrust dominant, moderate lapse.
        t = (u - f_counter) / (1.0 - f_counter)
        w_mix = 0.85 + 0.10 * t          # [0.85, 0.95]
        epsilon = 0.08 + 0.10 * t        # [0.08, 0.18]
        gamma = 1.5 + 1.5 * t            # [1.5, 3.0]
    w_mix = float(min(max(w_mix, 0.5), 0.95))

    # --- Route 1: raw validity-proportional distrust charge ---
    d = c0 + c1 * np.power(v_pow, kappa)
    pen_a = float(np.dot(d, a))
    pen_b = float(np.dot(d, b))

    # Residual micro-trust: a small validity-weighted endorsement
    # edge. logit(0.5) = 0 (coin-flip experts contribute nothing) and
    # the logit is CAPPED at 3 so perfect experts (v = 1.0) exert a
    # bounded pull (validated twice on the Exp-12 saturation assay).
    lg = np.clip(np.log(v_tr / (1.0 - v_tr)), 0.0, 3.0)
    trust = float(np.dot(lg, a - b))

    # D > 0 favors A (B carries more accumulated suspicion, net of
    # the small trust edge).
    D = (pen_b - pen_a) + alpha * trust
    p_skeptic_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * D))  # stable sigmoid

    # --- Route 2: graded endorsement-count preference ---
    cnt_a = float(np.sum(a))
    cnt_b = float(np.sum(b))
    p_count_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * gamma * (cnt_b - cnt_a)))

    # --- Dual-route mixture ---
    p_a = w_mix * p_skeptic_a + (1.0 - w_mix) * p_count_a
    p_a = float(min(max(p_a, 0.0), 1.0))
    p_core = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # Independent lapse: with probability epsilon pick uniformly.
    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)
next_theory.rationale: This edit follows the iter-4 critic's prescription directly, on top of the unchanged iter-1 GDRD base. (1) The logit cap clip(logit(v), 0, 3) in the micro-trust term is retained — it was validated twice (iter-2: Exp 12 = 0.8300; iter-4: 0.8275 vs real 0.8320) and is provably inert for all v <= 0.95, so it can only help Exp 12. (2) alpha, c1, kappa, c0, beta are kept EXACTLY at the iter-1 base values — three consecutive rejections have fully mapped the trade-offs of touching them, and the iter-4 postmortem showed those rejections were driven by evaluation noise swamping sub-noise edits, not by the cap. (3) THE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE: the uniform w in [0.80, 0.92] (with independent epsilon, gamma) is replaced by a BIMODAL two-component population implemented as a quantile transform of a single uniform parameter u_pop in [0, 1]: a ~12% 'counter' minority at w in [0.50, 0.62] with low lapse [0.05, 0.10] and decisive gamma in [2.0, 3.0], and an ~88% 'skeptic' majority at w in [0.85, 0.95] with epsilon in [0.08, 0.18] and gamma in [1.5, 3.0]. The key structural property (and the reason iters 2-3's uniform widening failed while this should succeed) is that the population-MEAN route weight is held at the calibrated base value E[w] ~ 0.86, so the well-fit point estimates on Exps 2-5, 7, 9 are essentially undamaged, while the between-subject variance explodes on exactly the assays where the real variances exceed the binomial floor by 4-12x: Exp 11 (counters sit near 0.5-0.6 on saturated-conflict cells vs skeptics near 0.82, reproducing both the real mean ~0.7875 and pulling var from 0.012 toward the real 0.0537), Exp 12 (var from 0.005 toward the real 0.0438), Exp 10 (the counter pole pulls the mean from 0.55 toward the real 0.5096 AND adds spread), Exp 1 (counters follow the TTB winner via the count route, adding ~0.004 super-binomial variance at only ~+0.01 mean cost), Exp 8 (counters sit near chance on matched-count cells — variance gain, small mean cost). The counter pole was chosen over a high-lapse or high-alpha pole because it is directionally CONSISTENT with the distrust majority on Exps 5 and 6 (the count route also avoids the endorsement-majority/top-cue option), so those near-fit assays are undamaged. (4) Calibration choices per the critic: minority fraction f = 0.12; the majority's epsilon is lowered to [0.08, 0.18] (mean 0.13, above the ~0.08 floor below which Exp 5's mean would drop under the real 0.1143) to keep the Exp 11/12 skeptic-pole means at target. (5) The between-subject variance was the only remaining discrepancy an order of magnitude larger than the ~±0.005 evaluation noise floor; every point-estimate error left in the portfolio is <= 0.05 and three rejections have shown the point portfolio sits at its in-family Pareto frontier. This mixture is the one in-family mechanism that attacks the variance structure without moving the means, and it is MORE faithful to the arbiter's original GDRD sketch (which explicitly prescribed w down to 0.5 and wide per-subject heterogeneity) than the narrowed iter-1 box.

experiment.rationale: NOVEL AXIS (vs. Exps 0-11): the first head-to-head between SVD (advocated) and GDRD-B (competing) — two theories that share the SAME distrust core (penalty c0 + c1*v^kappa, sigmoid comparison, lapse) AND, by construction, the same population-MEAN route weight (~0.86): GDRD-B's bimodal quantile transform explicitly holds E[w] at SVD's base value. A box-robust sign conflict is therefore provably impossible (the skeptic cores are near-identical and their boxes overlap), and pooled-mean gaps on any single cell are bounded at ~3 points. The dissociation must be fought on three quantitative fronts, all exploited here: (1) the SATURATION ASYMPTOTE LEVEL (a pure lapse assay: on cells where both branches saturate, P = 1 - E[eps]/2 — SVD .910 with every subject in [.874,.940]; GDRD-B .938 with NO subject below .899 and ~65% above .940); (2) a POOLED-MEAN DOUBLE CROSSING (GDRD-B is ABOVE SVD on saturated cells by its lower lapse, but BELOW SVD on single-vs-many exchange cells by its higher w and graded — not step — count route: an interaction no reparameterization can mimic, since eps and w push in opposite directions across the two families); (3) the PER-SUBJECT DISTRIBUTION (GDRD-B's 12% counter minority with w in [.50,.62] lands 8-20 points OUTSIDE SVD's box on count-conflict cells, producing the bimodality/super-binomial variance GDRD-B claims — turned here into its falsifiable liability: SVD bounds EVERY subject's conflict-cell rate >= .69 because w >= .80 and eps >= .12). VALIDITY ENGINEERING: 6 perfect experts (v=1.0) give the maximum, KAPPA-INVARIANT charge c0+c1 (closing every corner-escape route, as in Exp 11) and a capped logit (3) that bounds GDRD-B's micro-trust term at 0.15/endorsement vs a >= 0.6 per-pair charge gap — verified: saturation survives every corner of BOTH boxes including alpha=0.05; 8 coin experts (v=0.50) give the cheapest charge (c0+c1*0.5^k in [0.39,0.57]) and ZERO logit (alpha-inert); 2 experts at v=0.65 have a coin-charge ratio of 1.36-1.54 across BOTH entire boxes, making the 2-vs-3 penalty-matched cell residual |D| <= 0.14 (skeptic in [.44,.61]) by arithmetic. 8 base pairs, each exactly A/B-mirrored (16 unique pairs, K = 96//16 = 6, 96 trials, 12 samples per base cell per subject), perfectly side-balanced. Mid parameters quoted: SVD (c0=.085, c1=1.125, kappa=1.65, beta=1.9, w=.86, eps=.18); GDRD-B majority (c0=.095, c1=1.175, kappa=1.85, beta=1.9, w=.90, eps=.13, gamma=2.25, alpha=.025) and minority (w=.56, eps=.075, gamma=2.5); box ranges verified at box corners. FAMILY 1 — SATURATED CONFLICT / COUNTER-TAIL CELLS (pairs 1-2, primary): A = 8 (then 7) coin endorsements vs B = 6 (then 5) perfect endorsements. Skeptic evidence is saturated toward A at every corner of both boxes (|D| >= 2.16; SVD s_A >= .93, GDRD s_A >= .90 even after the worst alpha pull), while the count route saturates toward B (A carries MORE endorsements). SVD: P(A) = (1-eps)*w*s_A + eps/2, every subject in [.685,.870] (population ~.79). GDRD-B: skeptic majority [.72,.92], but the 12% counter minority lands in [.46,.62] — DISJOINT from SVD's box by >= 7 points on both pairs. FALSIFICATION: any subject with a pooled conflict-cell rate < .65 (24 trials) is outside SVD's entire box (w >= .80, eps >= .12, s >= .93 make it unreachable); conversely, ZERO such subjects in N >= 40 (P = .88^40 = 0.7% under GDRD-B) rejects the bimodal population outright. GDRD-B also predicts 2.2x super-binomial between-subject variance here (SD ~.10 vs SVD's ~.045). FAMILY 2 — ASYMPTOTE / LAPSE CELLS (pairs 3-4): A = 1 (then 2) coin endorsement vs B = 4 (then 5) perfect endorsements; both branches saturate toward A (|D| >= 3.6 at every corner), so P(A) = 1 - eps/2. SVD: every subject in [.874,.940], population .910. GDRD-B: skeptics >= .899, counters >= .937, population .938. A pooled asymptote <= .92 favors SVD; >= .925 favors GDRD-B (with 48 trials/subject and N >= 20 subjects the 2.8-point gap is > 4 SE). Additionally, > 40% of subjects with individual asymptote rates above .94 falsifies SVD (its eps >= .12 caps every subject at .940); a substantial fraction of subjects below .89 falsifies GDRD-B (its lowest possible subject is .899). FAMILY 3 — PARITY CAP CELL (pair 5): A = 5 perfects vs B = 5 coins; skeptic saturates toward B (the cheap side), counts matched so the count branch sits at exactly 0.5. P(B) = (1-eps)(1+w)/2 + eps/2: SVD [.79,.91] (pop .85); GDRD-B counters [.71,.80] — a second, independent location where the minority mode falls below SVD's floor. FAMILY 4 — PENALTY-MATCHED COUNT-STEP CELL (pair 6): A = 2x0.65 vs B = 3x0.50; the charge ratio pins the skeptic to s in [.44,.61] across both boxes while the count route votes A (fewer endorsements). SVD is squeezed into a remarkably tight window [.52,.65] (pop ~.585) because its eps and w effects offset; GDRD-B's counters rise to [.60,.77] (pop .567) — above SVD's ceiling — and its alpha term lets skeptics drift to .65 at extreme corners where SVD cannot exceed .61 in the opposite direction. FAMILY 5 — EXCHANGE CELLS (pairs 7-8): A = 1 perfect vs B = 2 (then 4) coins; these trace each theory's sigmoid for beta calibration and complete the mean double-crossing: SVD population P(A) = .45 and .72 vs GDRD-B .42 and .69 (GDRD-B's higher w and graded count route make it systematically LESS favorable to the single-endorsement side, ~3 points at both rungs; box-verified direction is stable at mid parameters, with corner overlap acknowledged — these are secondary cells). THE JOINT PROFILE IS UN-FAKEABLE: because GDRD-B holds E[w] at SVD's value, no single-cell reparameterization separates them — but the CONJUNCTION {asymptote level .91 vs .94, conflict-cell floor .69 vs a 12% mode at .49-.62, parity-cap floor .79 vs .71-.80, penalty-matched ceiling .65 vs .60-.77, exchange means .45/.72 vs .42/.69} is a profile neither box can approximate in the other's direction: SVD's eps >= .12 and w <= .92 bound every subject's asymptote <= .940 and conflict rate >= .685, while GDRD-B's skeptic eps <= .18 and counter w <= .62 bound its asymptote >= .899 and its minority's conflict rate <= .62; the two theories' per-subject envelopes are disjoint on Families 1-3 simultaneously, and the parameters trade off oppositely across families (the GDRD-B corner that best mimics SVD's asymptote, eps=.18, simultaneously deepens its conflict-cell divergence). POWER NOTE: the pooled-mean assays (Families 1-2) need only ~20 subjects; the distributional tail/bimodality assays need N >= 40-50 (detecting a 12% mode is inherently a large-N test — the design concentrates 24 conflict trials and 48 asymptote trials per subject to make per-subject rates estimable). PREDICTED OUTCOMES: an SVD population shows asymptote ~.91, zero subjects above .94, all conflict rates in [.69,.87], unimodal between-subject spread; a GDRD-B population shows asymptote ~.94, ~2/3 of subjects above .94, a distinct ~12% cluster at .49-.62 on conflict cells (and .60-.77 on pair 6, .44-.71 on pair 7), and super-binomial conflict-cell variance. All 16 pairs are non-degenerate (every pair has discriminating endorsements, both options carry >= 1 endorsement and >= 1 non-endorsement, no all-tie pairs, no pair where both theories guess — the closest cells, pairs 6-7, are exactly where the minority mode separates), and every trial requires actually comparing the two rating vectors. Both theories are history-free (validities in the instructions), so K=6 repetition is harmless.

metric.rationale: THE ASSAY. The 24 trials per subject built from pairs 3/4 and their mirrors 11/12 (one option carrying only 1-2 coin endorsements, the other only 4-5 perfect endorsements) saturate BOTH routes of BOTH theories toward the coin-side option: the skeptic's penalty difference is at least 3.2 logit-units at every corner of both parameter boxes (beta*D >= 4.2 even in the worst corner, including GDRD-B's micro-trust pull), and the count route also favors that side (fewer endorsements; GDRD-B's graded count is >= .989). So P(choose coin side) = 1 - epsilon/2 exactly: a pure, kappa/w/beta/alpha-invariant readout of each subject's lapse rate. THE PER-SUBJECT VALUE. metric(single subject) = that subject's saturation accuracy (rate of choosing the low-penalty side on these 24 trials). Under SVD, epsilon ~ U(.12,.24) puts every subject's TRUE accuracy in [.87,.93]. Under GDRD-B, the skeptic majority (epsilon in [.08,.18]) sits in [.90,.95] and the entire counter minority (epsilon in [.05,.10]) sits in [.94,.97]. This per-subject value is tightly distributed (variance ~ .004, dominated by ordinary binomial noise), which keeps the Welch denominator small. THE POPULATION SCALAR. metric(pooled data) = the prevalence of ceiling-level saturation: the fraction of subjects whose saturation accuracy is >= 95% (i.e., at most one non-ceiling choice in 24 trials). This is the falsification statistic the design was built around: SVD's epsilon >= .12 hard-caps every subject's true rate at ~.93, so ceiling performance can occur there only through binomial noise (~30% of subjects land at >= 23/24 by chance). GDRD-B puts roughly half the population genuinely at ceiling: about 40% of its skeptic majority (epsilon < .12) plus all of its low-lapse counter minority, for an expected prevalence near .48. The binomial tail P(X >= 23 | n=24) is steep exactly on the interval separating the two theories' lapse distributions (.90 vs .93 vs .95), which is why the prevalence converts the same underlying 2.5-3 point lapse difference that a raw mean-rate metric can barely resolve (per-subject rate SD ~ .06 gives t ~ 1.6 at N=25, below significance) into a ~18-point contrast with per-subject variance ~ .004, giving a Welch t around 10 at N=25. DIRECTION AND ROBUSTNESS. GDRD-B scores HIGHER (more ceiling saturators); SVD scores ~ .30.
